We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be 7 years of age by program start date.

 

NICA Discovery Little Rock meets at Camp Robinson and Two Rivers Bike Park on Tuesday evenings 5:00-6:30

October 13

October 20

October 27

November 3

November 10

November 17

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sing and bring it to the first session for their child to participate.  
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates.

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each session is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-session for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each session builds on skills learned in the previous session.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every session! 

For New Friends, the sessions consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

EventName: Women's Cycling Collective: FREE Virtual Live Introductory Classes - November 18th - 24th, 2026!
EventNotes:
WCC VELOCITY:

FREE WOMEN'S VIRTUAL CYCLING TRIAL CLASSES

November 18–20 & November 24, 2026

 

Curious about indoor cycling? Looking for a fun, motivating way to stay active, build fitness, and connect with other women through the winter?

 

Women's Cycling Collective (WCC) invites you to try FREE introductory virtual cycling classes using our WCC Velocity training platform!  Whether you're a seasoned cyclist, newer to structured training, or simply curious about virtual group workouts, there's a place for you here.

 

These sessions offer a chance to meet the WCC community, explore the Velocity platform, experience a group workout, and see if virtual winter training is right for you. Returning WCC athletes are welcome, too!

 

No experience with virtual training is necessary. Try something new. Build winter fitness. Find your people. Train together!

 

 

WHAT MAKES WCC VELOCITY DIFFERENT?

We train together, but we're individually challenged.

 

Everyone follows the same workout, but the workout targets are matched to each athlete's individual fitness level. Whether you're new to cycling or a seasoned rider, you can work at your own capacity, push your personal edges, and build strength and endurance alongside other women.

 

You get the motivation and connection of a group, with a training experience that's appropriate for YOU.

 

WHAT TO EXPECT THIS WINTER

WCC Virtual Winter Training is built around a structured, progressive training plan designed to develop fitness throughout the winter and prepare you for spring and summer riding.

  • Live, coach-led virtual cycling classes on select weekday mornings and evenings.
  • Group replay workouts for added scheduling flexibility.
  • A mix of endurance, interval, high-intensity, and mixed-intensity workouts.
  • A balanced approach that includes consistency, rest, and recovery.
  • Coaching feedback, encouragement, and connection with other women.

 

Training can complement your other winter activities, including skiing, snowboarding, running, hiking, and backcountry adventures.

 

Our goal is to help you head into the 2027 cycling season feeling stronger, more confident, and ready to pursue your own goals—from local group rides and personal PRs to longer gravel events and A-races.

 

FREE NOVEMBER INTRODUCTORY CLASSES

Dates: November 18 (AM+PM), 19 (AM+PM), 20 (AM only) & 24 (AM+PM), 2026

Class times (Eastern):

  • Morning: 7:15–8:15 AM
  • Evening: 5:30–6:30 PM

 

Join as many sessions as you like! You can participate in the workout or simply observe and learn.

 

During these sessions, we'll help you:

  • Learn about and navigate the WCC Velocity app and dashboard.
  • Understand how to prepare for and participate in a virtual class.
  • Explore different workout formats.
  • Experience a guided group workout.
  • Meet other women interested in winter training.

Please arrive on time for the introduction. You're welcome to leave early if needed.

 

Registration and setup: You'll need to create your free Velocity account at least 48 hours before your first session. Setup instructions will be emailed by Sunday, November 15. No payment or credit card is required. There is no obligation to join the winter program.

 

EQUIPMENT NEEDED

To participate fully, you'll need:

  • A compatible smart trainer or indoor bike that transmits power and cadence and supports app-controlled resistance and manual gear shifting. (Zwift Hubs will work if that is what you currently have, but it is recommended to purchase a trainer with manual gear shifting (non-Zwift hub) if making a new purchase.)
  • A compatible device to run the Velocity app.
  • Reliable internet and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) or ANT+ connectivity.
  • A heart rate monitor (strongly recommended).
  • A fan, water bottle, and towel.

 

A stable internet connection is important, particularly for classes using two-way video. Ethernet connection is recommended when possible.

 

Not sure if your equipment is compatible? Reach out! We're happy to help you figure out your setup before the winter season.

 

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER NOVEMBER?

Our official WCC Virtual Winter Training season launches in December 2026 and continues into spring 2027.

 

Membership options will include live coach-led classes, group replay workouts, and additional on-demand training opportunities. We're developing flexible membership options to accommodate different schedules, goals, and budgets, with anticipated basic memberships ranging from approximately $80–130. Final schedules and pricing will be announced separately.

 

TRAIN TOWARD SOMETHING!

Looking for a 2027 goal to motivate your winter training? WCC offers two supported women's gravel events:

  • WCC Century Litha Women's Gravel – 50/100 miles, southwestern Addison County, Vermont, June 19, 2027.
  • WCC Century Jubilee Women's Gravel – 22/50/100 miles, Hinesburg, Vermont, October 2, 2027.

Both events offer supportive, success-based environments where women can challenge themselves, learn, grow, and celebrate what they're capable of.

 

MEET YOUR COACH: LIZ

Liz is a National Board-Certified Health and Wellness Coach, Certified BICP Level 1 Mountain Bike Coach, co-founder of Women's Drop Ride, and founder of Women's Cycling Collective. After decades of wondering what it might be like to train and compete, she began her own focused gravel and mountain bike racing journey at age 47 and went on to win the overall Women's Open category at Unbound 200 at age 50. 

 

Her focus has turned towards supporting others by creating opportunities for women to explore and push their limits.  Through Women's Cycling Collective, she offers virtual training through the winter months and highly supported in-person 100/50mi gravel events specifically for women.

 

Her coaching philosophy is rooted in meeting athletes where they are, helping them discover their own goals, and supporting their individual growth. She believes training goes far beyond the bike: it's an opportunity to build confidence, challenge perceived limits, and cultivate fitness of mind, body, and heart.

 

Liz is passionate about helping women develop what she calls soft ferocity—the courage to explore our potential, embrace challenges, and remain true to ourselves. She believes success is not a finite resource to be divided or competed for, but something that grows when women support, encourage, and inspire one another.

 

 

COME RIDE WITH US!

You don't need to be the strongest rider in the room. You don't need years of experience or prior virtual training experience. 

 

Come as you are. Train at your own level. Find your community. Discover what's possible when women ride together.

 

Same workout. Your own edge. Stronger as a collective.

 

We can't wait to meet you and ride with you!

 

Looking forward,

Liz Wolf
Women's Cycling Collective

The Donderdag! Youth Cyclocross Clinics are open to any youth rider eager to build confidence, make friends, and experience the excitement of cyclocross!

Our mission is to provide a safe, supportive, and fun environment where kids can develop fundamental bike handling skills, practice bike safety, and enjoy the outdoors with good food and great community. While we introduce clear, simple skills to help those interested in racing, our primary goal is helping every rider grow their strength, agility, and self-belief on two wheels. We encourage participants to show up ready to learn, support their peers, and simply give their personal best each week.

Driven by dedicated volunteers, Donderdag! fosters community leadership and mentorship. Teen riders are coached to guide and protect younger participants, while local volunteers help build a welcoming, inclusive cycling culture. Through our core coaching framework—Balance, Agility, Strength, and Exposure (B.A.S.E.)—riders gain lifelong skills that bring both confidence on the trail and success on race day.

Ultimately, Donderdag! exists to remind our community of the grace, connection, and strength found in grassroots coaching, leadership, and serving others.

EventNotes:
Space Cowboy Cross!

The Houston Round of the State CX series
Presented by 

Shoot for the stars at Space Cowboy Cyclocross at the Pasadena Convention Center and Municipal Fairgrounds in Pasadena, TX – Part of the  TXCX series.

 If you are going to CX Nationals in Fayetteville, AR, Dec 10–14, 2025, earn USA Cycling points at this race and improve your starting position there.

Course Notes– packed with off-camber turns, and fast, flowy sections. Alligators optional.

Spectator-friendly - Plenty of parking, and most of the course is viewable from the finish area.

Want to try cyclocross? There is a category for everyone, including first-time racers.

 

Race rules:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. All USAC cyclocross rules apply.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced. 
  5. Please inform the officials if you withdraw from the race.

Entry Fees

EventName: Arkansas Enduro Series Finale | Round 4 | Mt. Nebo Enduro
EventNotes:
MT. NEBO ENDURO | NOVEMBER 21-22, 2026

We’re excited to return to the stunning Mount Nebo State Park! The Mt. Nebo Enduro is a mix of technical and flowy singletrack with stages for all levels. Perched high above the Arkansas River Valley, Mount Nebo offers amazing views.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Mount Nebo is a prominent, flat-topped mountain mesa located in west-central Arkansas near Dardanelle. Rising 1,762 feet above sea level and soaring 1,350 feet directly out of the surrounding Arkansas River Valley, it is entirely enclosed by Mount Nebo State Park. Established in 1927, it serves as Arkansas's second-oldest state park and is a premier hub for outdoor recreation. 

Venue Address: 16728 West State Hwy. 155, Dardanelle, AR 72834

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

FRIDAY |

  • Early pre-riding is allowed although some stages may in the proccess of being finishing marking.
  • 4PM-7PM | Early Check-In | Location TBA

SATURDAY |

  • 9AM-4PM | Check-In & Official Practice Day

SUNDAY | 

  • 8AM-10AM | Timing Chip Pick-Up according to Wave Times. Late Check-In available.
  • 9AM-3PM | Race Day
  • 4PM | Podium Awards

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

DRY CAMPING - To book your campsite, visit the Arkansas State Parks reservation page. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In November, Mount Nebo, Arkansas experiences cool, crisp weather. Temperatures typically reach an average high in the mid-50s (50°F to 54°F) and drop to average nightly lows in the low-to-mid 30s (30°F to 35°F).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

If participants choose to add additional Registration Protector through BikeReg, those claims are handled entirely by Allianz Global Assistance. For policy questions or to file a claim visit www.eventregistrationprotection.com or call 1-888-799-2832.

SERIES RULES - additional series information and rules available at www.arkansasenduroseries.com/rules.

Every year an event comes along that tests mental and physical strengths of its racers like no other. Pisgah Productions proudly presents the hardest (and most fun) thing you will do this year….. the DOUBLE DARE.

Teams of two riders will race to reach up to 10 checkpoints (CPs) per day, two days in a row. The race begins at 10AM on Saturday and every team must be back before 10PM. The race resumes at 6AM Sunday with 10 brand new checkpoints. Every team must finish before 6PM on Sunday. Teams ‘in the running’ should expect up to 70 miles of riding with 12,000-15,000 feet of climbing each day.

SINGLE-DARE! The one-day category at Double-Dare!!! Teams of two riders will race up to 10 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish the fastest. Checkpoint locations will remain secret until start time and there is no suggested route. Start time for the one-day category will be 10AM Saturday and Final cutoff will be 10PM.

For both DOUBLE-DARE and SINGLE-DARE:

There will be nothing at the checkpoints other than pre-existing landmarks. Every team must carry a reliable digital camera to photograph the landmarks as proof of being there.

Welcome to the Cross of the North registration page.  Come celebrate with us at New Belgium in Fort Collins for two days of exciting racing. For all of the event info, LIKE us on Facebook and FOLLOW us on Instagram and Twitter.

Also, please consider volunteering. It takes more than a village to make Cross of the North a success. Check out our volunteer signup.

Two things that you can refrain from to help ensure COTN's future at New Belgium:

In addition, all proceeds from alcohol sales are donated to support youth cycling through Send Town Bike Club!!
  • Do not park in the Buckingham neighborhood. Do not park or warm up on 1st, 2nd, or 3rd streets, on the south side of Buckingham, or any of the cross streets in the Buckingham neighborhood. New Belgium brings a lot of traffic to the neighborhood, and we want to respect their desire for peace and quiet.

1) 18 and Under race free, in Jr Categories and for $20 in any other categories.  Enter coupon code COTNJR2026 when you register.

2) Participants are required to have USA Cycling license. For SM 5, SW 5 and junior categories only, USA Cycling 1-day Beginner Licenses ($15) are available for purchase. 1-day licenses are available only to racers who have never held a USAC license with a higher category, Men/Junior Men and Women/Junior Women. USAC 1-Day Experienced license: $35, only available to former USAC members- category 1,2,3,4 men/women, and must be purchased online.

They may also enter categorized races for men that are up to one category lower than their women's category. For cyclo-cross events, category 1 women may enter men’s races up to two categories lower.

Master women may compete in men’s masters races as follows:

When registering for Men’s races, especially those in a lower category, you may receive a warning message. Please acknowledge the message and complete the registration.

Race day registration and packet pickup close 45 minutes before each race group. NO EXCEPTIONS.

Adding a second race on the same day is only $20.

Riding without first signing a waiver, or failing to follow race staff instructions, may result in disqualification from the Saturday and/or Sunday races.

At the discretion of the chief referee, some waves may be split into separate categories and begin on separate whistles. Can you believe it’s our eighteenth year! Join us for Turkey Bike on  Saturday November 21st. If you haven't done Turkey Bike before here's how it works. Riders meet at Cycle Craft in Parsippany and roll out at 9:00 and head to King’s supermarket in Boonton to buy a bunch of turkeys. Then, we ride over to Smartworld Coffee in Denville where the Community Food Bank of New Jersey is there to receive the birds. The ride is fairly easy and you only have to carry your turkey for a few miles. We recommend using a sturdy back pack or pannier bags on a rack to carry your bird. String bags are not any fun to use and front baskets can be tricky to manage with a 20lb turkey in it. There is no entry fee so your only cost is the cost of the turkey that you pick out.

When you arrive at Smartworld we'll treat to you hot beverages and delicious snacks as our way of saying "thanks!" for participating. Riders then head back to Cycle Craft. It's a fun way to do something good!

Riders meet at Cycle Craft Parsippany with check in beginning at 8:00AM and the ride rolls at 9:00AM. If you have any questions please email brendan@cyclecraft.com

If you can't make the ride please consider making a $35 donation and we will buy and carry your turkey for you!

Here is a link to the Turkey Bike Route  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/44981418 It says 2024 but the route is the same this year
PresentedBy: Cycle Craft & The Community Food Bank of New Jersey

Cranksgiving Boise is an annual alleycat-style scavenger hunt on bikes. Teams of costumed cyclists ride around town on an odyssey to find the answers to trivia questions about local art and history, while also gathering all the items necessary to fill Thanksgiving food boxes that will be donated to Saint Vincent de Paul for its program that helps feed families in need throughout the Treasure Valley. This is the 11th Annual edition of this fun biking event. 

Cranskgiving Boise will take place on Saturday, November 21st, starting and ending at  Idaho River Sports, 601 N Whitewater Park Blvd., Boise.  Packet pick-up starts at 10:00 a.m., with the event starting promptly at 11:00 a.m.

The ideal Cranksgiving team is four people. While teams can have up to six riders, if you have more riders than that, we strongly encourage you to create another team. The goal is to feed as many families as possible and having more teams helps achieve that goal. 

We are charging a modest $10 to register a team to cover our costs of hosting registration on this website and other expenses involved with staging this event.

Costumes are encouraged! There will be prizes for the first three teams by time, for the team bringing in the biggest turkey, and the teams with the best costumes, as decided by a vote of participants.

Cranksgiving is made possible this year by the generous support of Ketlinski Law Office.

For the latest information on Cranksgiving Boise, visit our Facebook page.
PresentedBy: Lost River Cycle Club and Ketlinski Law

EventName: Martha’s Vineyard Adventure Tour with Mike and Mary
EventNotes:
COME Ride Martha’s Vineyard with MTB legends, Mike and Mary - along with our friends of New England Expedition Riders (NEER)!  It will be a fun day of exploring the island’s back routes and trails on mountain or gravel bikes … We will ride a steady pace, intermediate to advanced - over mixed terrain with options to do shorter or longer routes depending on the crew…@25-30 miles…3-4 hours of GOOD Mixed terrain BIKE FUN :-)  

Details : We will meet around 10:30am in Vineyard Haven near the ferry, (off island riders can catch a 9:30am ferry (from Woods Hole).  We should be back from our ride around 3-3:30pm - so a 3:45pm or 5pm ferry back would be the earliest return).

It is an incredibly quiet and beautiful time of year to ride bikes!  

The route plan : A new configuration of quiet back routes through forest woodlands and to some gorgeous vantage points... We will take mid ride refreshment breaks and return back to our starting spot, for libations and a bowl of something hot around 3pm.   It is a no drop ride.

There will be ride leaders in the case we need to split into smaller groups.  GPS route will be available.

This ride will be operated with our friend Patria of New England Expedition Riders (NEER).  For Insurance purposes, we are requiring NEER membership in the  registration cost.

To register and purchase your annual NEER membership visit:

https://www.newenglandexpeditionriders.com/rides-events/mv-adventure-2025

or click the BIKE reg links

NEER is a fantastic group of hearty riders who love to get our all year round! Check them out!

Bikes:  we recommend MTBs (hardtail or dual suspension if you prefer to not feel the bumps ;-)). A Gravel bike with minimum 38-40mm tires is possible too!  We would like to get out on more trails than in past editions… It will not be an overly technical ride - but our island trails can be bumpy and leaves are down so larger volume tires are preferred for comfort….

There will be 2 mechanics on the ride (MIKE and Patria ;-) and We will have our tool kits on us (and a floor pump in our van…for before the ride) if needed...  

Please bring your bike in perfect working order…. and what you need to have a successful ride.  

Helmets are mandatory….and blinking RED taillights if you have it.  

Bring two h20 bottles and any special foods you ride with, and $ in the case we stop at a local establishment to refuel.

Bathrooms located at the Ferry Ticket Office. And along the way we will have some pit stops…

We recommend bringing warm cozy clothes for morning ferry over and hanging out at our beautiful start/finish location after... There will be a possibility to store your day pack in a safe place during our ride... 

More details upon registration...

Please email with any questions!

mikeandmaryride@gmail.com
PresentedBy: Mary McConneloug, Michael Broderick and New England Expedition Riders (NEER)

Go Nuts Regionals (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows: 
1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.
2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.
3) Studded tires are prohibited.
4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.
5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.
6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.
7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro. 
8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.
9) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.
10) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.
11) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.
12) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.
13) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.
15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.
16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.
17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.
The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

About USA Cycling and the NCNCA

USA Cycling (USAC) is the designated national governing body for the sport of cycling under the umbrella of the United States Olympic Committee (USOC). All Olympic sports follow the rules and regulations set forth in the USOC charter, and competitive cycling in the United States operates within this structure.

To better support riders, officials, promoters, and events across the country, USA Cycling divides the nation into regional districts. The Northern California Nevada Cycling Association (NCNCA) is the USA Cycling–recognized Local Association for the Northern California/Nevada region.

Whether you are new to the sport or a world-class athlete competing at the National, Pan American, World, or Olympic level, you participate within the support framework of USA Cycling, the USOC, and your Local Association — the NCNCA.

What the NCNCA Does

The NCNCA is a nonprofit, membership-based regional athletic association that supports competitive cycling and community-building across Northern California and Nevada. As the Local Association for USAC, the NCNCA is responsible for:

  • Coordinating and publishing the regional calendar of USA Cycling–sanctioned events
  • Supporting and training USA Cycling–licensed officials
  • Assisting promoters with event permitting and post-event reporting
  • Maintaining and providing event equipment to local promoters (finish-line cameras, timing equipment, traffic control gear, laptops, etc.)
  • Managing the region’s BAR/BAT season-long competition and race results
  • Supporting safety, fairness, and quality at all sanctioned events

The NCNCA’s ability to provide these services relies heavily on the support of its member clubs.

Membership and Club Support Levels

The NCNCA is governed by an elected Board of Directors. Member clubs contribute directly to the association’s annual operating budget. These contributions enable the NCNCA to maintain equipment, develop officials, run series competitions, support riders and promoters, and deliver high-quality racing experiences.

Clubs are invited to join at the following levels:

  • Gold Level – $500+
  • Silver Level – $250
  • Bronze Level – $150

All levels directly support the NCNCA’s mission: to maintain the highest standards of organization, safety, inclusion, development, and competition for riders, promoters, and the broader cycling community.

Membership Benefits by Support Tier

Membership-Wide Benefits (All Clubs)

Regardless of support tier, all NCNCA-affiliated clubs receive:

  • A comprehensive, year-round NCNCA event calendar with links to flyers, registration, and course maps
  • Conflict mitigation and scheduling coordination to maximize event success
  • Timely posting of results and standings for BAR/BAT and development series
  • Monthly newsletter and regular communication through social media and email
  • Oversight, rule enforcement, and the presence of trained officials at permitted events
  • A regional network that promotes safe, fair, and well-organized competition across all disciplines

These baseline services are funded by club contributions, USA Cycling Local Association support, grants, and volunteer effort.

Our Commitment

The NCNCA exists to support its members — riders, clubs, promoters, officials, and the cycling community at large. Our mission is to deliver a positive, inclusive, and high-quality cycling experience for athletes of every level.

Your team’s participation and financial support make this work possible. Together we can continue to grow and strengthen cycling in Northern California and Nevada.

  • Discounts and special team pricing on goods and services from team sponsors: Trek, Stein Home Improvement, HealthQuest, Wolfson, Bolton, Kochis PLLC, Human Brand, Industrial Metal Sales, CTS, Cold Stone, Industry Nine, White Pine Coffee.
  • Inclusion on our Mitten Velo email group. This is a great source for ride information and other things.
     

Team Member Responsibilities:

  • Pay annual dues in the amount of $75.00 (the “Dues”) for the 2026 calendar year when your application is submitted or as otherwise required herein along with a signed Release, Assumption of Risk and Indemnification Agreement, which is included with your BikeReg registration. Team members accepted after the set deadline will be based solely upon the discretion of the Team Manager.
  • Participate in races and training rides to generate publicity for the Sponsors and the Team. You are expected to represent the Team with pride, professionalism, and good sportsmanship at all times. Our goal is to welcome all riders at our group rides and help educate new riders when it comes to the rules of the road. We’re striving to build and maintain rides that offer a great experience to all riders.
  • Volunteer during the year to assist in the organization and running of: Team rides, race events, or in-store promotions. This may be in the form of working a demo, race, promotional event, educational in-store clinics, test-rides with riders in season, coaching high school teams, etc.
  • Support the Sponsors by wearing the Mitten Velo kit in your races. Team members will set an example to other cyclists and the community by wearing a helmet and obeying all traffic laws. 
  • All racing entrants will list Mitten Velo on their USAC license, race registration when entering events and wear approved team apparel in all races and events. 
  • Team members will not approach Team Sponsors requesting individual or additional sponsorship monies.
  • Team members will properly enter races and events and pay the appropriate entry fees. No “bandit” racing.
  • Each Team member should post on their social media throughout the year. Primary platforms include Facebook and/or Instagram.
  • Failure to fulfill any of these responsibilities is cause for termination of this Agreement and dismissal from the Team, at the Team Manager’s sole discretion.

2026 Team/Member Focus & Goals:

FAQs:

  1. Do you accept anyone who applies?
    1. No we do not. We prefer quality over quantity. We’re just like-minded individuals who enjoy being able to participate in the fun rides and races we do and overall just love riding bikes.
  2. Is Cold Stone still part of the team?
    1. Yes! Todd and Cold Stone are still part of the team and will be offering the same great ice cream to all of us. 
  3. Do I have to race?
    1. No, you don’t. Most of us do race and the goal of the team is to work and train for races, but racing is not required to be accepted. Note: if you are interested in racing but aren’t sure where to start, let us know. We have team members happy to help you get started. 
  4. Do I need to wear the Mitten Velo kit all the time?
    1. We’d love you to, as much as possible, but please ensure you can for your races. I mean, you’re here applying to be on the team, right? 
  5. How should I list Mitten Velo on Strava and on BikeReg for events?
    1. Optionally, you're welcome to add “@Mitten Velo Racing” to your Strava name. And for BikeReg, please use “Mitten Velo Racing” for the team name under your profile.
  6. How can I get Mitten Velo helmet or bike stickers?

    1. Let someone on the BOD know and we’ll help you through it.

The mission of the Thread City Cyclers (TCC) is to provide opportunities for cyclists of various skill levels to ride together and to challenge themselves physically in a manner that builds individual performance, teamwork, and goodwill among club members.

The goals of the club are to:

  • Promote cycling in Connecticut and other locations where TCC activities may take us.
  • Develop riding skills
  • Provide a framework for like-minded individuals to train and socialize
  • Sponsor and support local cycling events including races, group rides, skill clinics, and overnight trips

TCC is a sanctioned club of the League of American Bicyclists

 

Dues

·         Dues are $30/year/person and $50/year/family (2+ people from the same household).

TCC Rules of the Ride

Due to inherent danger of this sport, TCC is not responsible for, and maintains no liability for any injury incurred during a club ride.

The following Rules of the Ride apply to all TCC sponsored rides and events:

1.     All traffic laws are to be obeyed (These include but are not limited to stop signs, traffic lights, yellow lines, as well as trail rules)

2.     Helmets are required on all TCC club rides.

3.     Single file riding is mandatory in heavy traffic and where conditions warrant.

4.     Sprinting and high intensity portion of training rides allowed only where traffic conditions permit 

5.     Absolutely no comment, hand gesture, etc. in reaction to automobile driver/passenger actions.

6.     Ride as far to the right as it is safe, and always to the right side of the yellow/centerline of the road.

7.     Use hand and verbal signals to notify other riders, as well as cars, of intent, road hazards, etc.

8.     Riders are not to be dropped at stop signs, lights, or during mechanical breakdowns.

9.     Intent of ride (Training, fitness, tempo) should and will be advertised prior to the start of the ride. If you aren’t sure about the ride plan – please ask before the ride leaves the assembly point.

Violation of these rules creates a danger for yourself and others on the ride. If you choose to violate any of these ride rules, the violation will be addressed by the ride leader as a warning. Repeat offense will result in a pro-rated refund of your club dues, acting as a severance of your club membership.

         Please remember: Every time you ride in your TCC uniform, on a club ride or by yourself, you are identifiable and representative of TCC. The driver that crowds you, and then sees your salutation or the one who watches you disobey basic traffic laws could be the same driver that then puts the next TCC jersey he sees in the ditch. We want to build respect for our sport and our club, and we know that these goals will serve to complement your personal goals, not hinder them in any way.  As a member of TCC you are acknowledging that you understand and are willing to ride within these guidelines.

Welcome to the Green Mountain Bicycle Club!

Founded in the winter of 1970/71, GMBC is the oldest bicycle club in Vermont and sits among the oldest in the country.

The mission of GMBC is to promote safe riding practices, sharing the road, and following state laws pertaining to bicycles (i.e., stopping at stop signs/lights and not to impede traffic flow).

The road is full of dangers, and to mitigate these, GMBC encourages all cyclists to mount a bright rear flasher (and a front one is recommended as well, especially if riding on busy roads), to wear bright clothing and a helmet, use arm signals, to stop at stop signs/lights – or at least to slow to a crawl – and to mount a mirror.

GMBC offers rides from April to November and competitive events from May to August. Join the club’s listserv to receive event announcements or visit the online calendar.

GMBC in the Community

  • In the spring it offers several Intro to Riding training sessions.
  • Is a supporting organization of Local Motion and has worked with it in the past on safe-cycling advocacy/initiatives.
  • Raised over $2,000 for restoration of the Island Line Trail after it was damaged by record flooding of Lake Champlain.
  • Aided a citizen advocate in his attempt to have an enhancement made to the Safe Passing guidance.
  • Played a key role in the inclusion of text in the VT Driver's Manual on how to pass bicyclists.
  • Made suggestions on rewording of state statutes related to bicyclists.
  • Was invited to and took part in a VTrans initiative to improve state roads for bicycle travel.

Note on the BikeReg Fee Charged

  • GMBC is covering half of the fee that BikeReg charges on each membership sold.

What to Expect After You Purchase a Membership

  • A purchase confirmation email from BikeReg.
  • An email welcoming you to the club, with your ID card(s) attached, and information on GMBC (this is a manual step, and it may take several weeks or more).

Info on Lifetime Memberships

  • You are responsible for notifying GMBC if your email address or emergency contacts info changes. Email updates to thegmbc@gmavt.net.
  • However, at the beginning of each year, an email will be sent to the email address associated with the membership asking for verification of demographic and emergency contacts data.
  • After confirmation is received, an ID card(s) for the current year will be emailed.

EventNotes:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ About STAGE 1 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

      

Welcome! The Stage 1 Cycling Club is a registered non-profit cycling organization based in East Hampton, CT. We got our start over 30 years ago here in Connecticut and have gone through many iterations and changes over the years. But one constant remains: STAGE 1 is dedicated first and foremost to having fun, building a community of cyclists where all riders are welcome, and promoting the sport of bicycling across the region. We believe that pretty much everyone is happier on a bike, whether riding or racing on the road, the mountain, on gravel, or snow -- it's all about the fun! 

STAGE 1 is composed of riders of all levels from all walks of life, from beginners to elite racers. If you don’t know how to ride a bike, we’ll teach you. If you’re a national level competitor, we’ll support you and help make you better. Most of all, we want to ride with you. To join STAGE 1, please contact us first through our Facebook page, or drop by AirLine Cycles in East Hampton, CT, so we can talk with you, tell you more about our club, and learn more about you and your goals. Better yet, join us for a ride and lets talk more over pizza and a drink. No race resumes, no secret handshakes - just a good attitude and a desire to ride. If we're the right fit for you, welcome aboard! Just come on back here, and you can complete the registration process. Of course, if you want in now, that's fine too! 

STAGE 1 members receive discounts from our sponsors, and the more committed our riders and members are, the more sponsorship they receive. Unlike many teams, it’s not just about results: it’s about commitment, attitude, and effort.

STAGE 1 is currently made up of over 100 full members: about 60 seniors, 35 juniors, 20 women and girls (we’d love to see more!); our oldest member is 70 and our youngest is 5. 

We are an active club and we host many cycling events each year.  Obviously 2020/21 were COVID years, but we still managed to put on several COVID-safe events . Moving forward, we plan to host our USAC sanctioned mountain bike & cross races. Of course, we will also hold many training rides, fun rides, and competitive road adventure and gravel rides. And together with AirLine Cycles, we host a Thursday night mountain bike training ride (year around) and Wednesday night gravel ride (during the summer). And, of course, we will continue with our popular junior programs and activities.

What else?  Well, we race a lot! STAGE 1 riders participate in events all over New England and you will also find us competing in the mid-Atlantic, California, and other locations all over the country racing nearly every weekend in the spring, summer, and fall (sometime in the winter too). Although we are heavily mountain and cyclocross focused at the moment, we also compete in road events and multi-sport competition. We proudly sponsor a junior team and we are committed to getting as many kids on bikes as possible!  If you join us and plan to seek a USAC license, please be sure to indicate your club affiliation as STAGE 1 Cycling Club (STAGE 1/AirLine Cycles). You can purchase a race license here: https://www.usacycling.org/.

But plenty of our active members don’t race and that’s fine too. We're glad to hangout and party with all comers! 

We have great sponsors who generously support our club and believe in our mission. They are AirLine Cycles, Fat Orange Cat Brewery, and Pactimo.

Come join us and have some fun!

EventNotes:
Welcome to the 2026 Spring Session of Galbraith Gravity Racing!

Important - Getting Started:

  1. Sign up for a race license at USA Cycling prior to registering, the system will ask for your USAC license number.  
  2. When signing up for your USA Cycling license - add Galbraith Gravity Racing as your team affiliation.  Any issues with USA Cycling are easily fixed by emailing: membership@usacycling.org
  3. Your GGR Team membership includes discounted entry to all six GGR Galbraith Grassroots Racing presented by Transition Bikes local races - you still need to register for each race - this is how we assign race plate numbers and sign race waivers.

Coaches start training in February depending on the weather.  All other racers will start the GGR spring session the week of 09 March through 21 May 2026.  A 10 week program.  The week of 25 May is an optional make up week based on weather, budget, and how the team is feeling!   Registration includes:

  • Racer jersey
  • Discounted entry fees for all six GGR races.
  • 10 weeks of practice with 6 weeks of local GGR racing (we take breaks for Spring Break)
  • Race Support at races noted on the GGR race calendar
  • Race support and team events through June 15th 2023.
  • Access to team pits at all races the team attends - and access to team pit equipment and race trailer.
  • Use of the team huck wagon and team shuttle days.
  • Fall program will require additional registration.  
  • Any Spring Break and Summer Camps will require separate registration.
  • Year round access to the team SLACK, What'sApp and Calendar
  • All trailers wagons, equipment etc are subject to restrictions.  This is a race team - stuff happens so be flexible.
  • Team discounts from team sponsors.

The goal of the spring session is to practice key skills, build confidence, team cohesion, endurance and experience the fun of racing.  Racers practice for two weeks, then practice/race for six weeks.  During the session we have trips to Port Angeles WA for NW Cup #1 & #2 (not mandatory), and take the week off for Spring Break.  The team my conduct a Spring Break Camp and a Summer Camp prior to the NW Tune Up for an additional registration.  During the session, try racing the NW Cup Race #1 & #2 and/or the first two Cascadia Dirt Cups.  

The season training calendar is pointed straight at Hot Laps MTB Festival and races presented by friends of the team Jill Kintner and Matt Orlando.  The following week is the National Enduro Champsionship in Silver Mountain - Many of our racers are going for it.  Last year 2025 saw GGR Coach Nash Jamieson win the U16 Category!

When the session is over - racers head off and complete the races they want to make in the summer.  Let's take that  a GGR to win the NW Cup Overall again in 2026!

Please note:

  • Dates are weather and safety dependent, changes can and will occur.  We reserve the right to cancel practice/races and makeup dates may not be available.
  • Specific dates for specific age groups will be posted on the team calendar and on the team SLACK message board.
  • Nothing is mandatory to attend - racers set their own schedule
    • All racers must agree to the code of conduct.
    • GGR is a race team - not a child care service or full service coaching clinic program.  Everyone is expected to contribute, be flexible, and help the team.  Fees are used to pay insurance, buy equipment, purchase coaching certifications, etc.  This is not fee for service - in other words, we do not offer prorated refunds.

Calendar (age group groups will be moved about based on the racers needs.  We will offer a M-W option and a T-TH option for practices. Racers can mix and match on a limited basis with approval.  Times are based on sunset, but basically start a little after 4:30ish.  Some rides can happen early for smaller kids based on coach availability.  Some Monday rides are not available after NW Cup events.  Groups are made up after registration)

  • Feb - coaching clinics
  • Week of 3/9: two skill practice sessions
  • Week of 3/16: one skill practice, one race course practice, GGR Saturday Race 1
  • Week of 3/23: one skill practice, one race course practice, GGR Saturday Race 2
  • Week of 3/30: one skill practice, one race course practice, GGR Saturday Race 3
  • 4/7: Spring Break - End of Week is NW Cup 1.  Some Elite Sessions planned with BluePrint.  Possible camp
  • Week of 4/13: two skill practice sessions, no practice on 4/13, GGR Saturday Race 4
  • Week of 4/20: one skill practice, one race course practice, GGR Saturday Race 5
  • Week of 4/27: one skill practice, one race course practice, GGR Saturday Race 6 (Finals)
  • Week of 5/4: two skill practice sessions, CDC 1
  • Week of 5/11: two skill practice sessions, NW Cup 1, no practice 5/14
  • Week of 5/19: Monday 5/18 off, 2X Practice Week, CDC 2
  • Week of 5/25: GGR Makup Week
  • May 29-31 Hot Laps MTB Fesitval
  • June 6-7-8 NAEC Silver Mountain.
  • Note:  GGR races, NAEC, Hot Laps, CDC and NW Cup require their own separate registration.

Registering through BikeReg allows us to electronically complete waivers for all our participants, connects to USA Cycling and more. Creating a BIKEREG account when signing for membership will make it easier for signing up to races/clinic etc.  NW Cup also uses BIKEREG, so create an account if you don't already have one - it will save time in the future. 

AGE Groups.  U13, U11, U8 train T/Th.  U15, U17, U19 train M/W.   Age is determined as of December 31, 2026. Please note: The terms that NW Cup uses are a little different than the ones we use and the UCI uses.  NW Cup would use U7 (=U8), U10 (=U11), U12 (=U13), U14 (=U15), U16 (=U17), U18 (=U19).  But we align with USAC, UCI and Canada.
 

***Please note - The event title is 'Membership Drive'.  The timeframe for membership is not the term of membership.  Team insurance and membership set to cover the entire year, through Dec 31st, 2023.  The training and riding spring session season is planned to be Feb-May and team membership is through October, but many factors are considered and the riding schedule is not final.

***Please note - The event title is 'Membership Drive'.  The timeframe for membership is not the term of membership.  Team insurance and membership set to cover the entire year, and this memebrship lasts until the beginning of the fall registration, date TBD, but you are always welcome at the team pits for any races in the fall.

When you join - you will gain electronic access to the team calendar and team SLACK/What'sApp platform - access emails are not automatic, we have to put them in manually, feel free to remind us.

Membership also includes team jersey for the racers, parents need to purchase a jersey if they want one.  Parents are encouraged to race in a team jersey!  We have a specific support group for parents for 'kids that are faster than they are' ;).  Once into SLACK/What'sApp and the Calendar, you will see season training seminars that start early March.  These seminars are the fundamentals racers will practice over and over...  The season is divided into three main parts - Training in the Spring (Spring Session).  Racing in the Summer (NW Cups, Cascadia Enduros, BMEs, Nationals etc).  Taper and fun in the Fall.  If you have questions - please let us know.

Refunds - we have fixed and variable costs. If you change your mind, and need a refund, funds may not be available. Once clinics start, and jerseys have been ordered no refunds for these items will be issued.  

Appreciate your being part of the team!

The New Orleans Bicycle Club is an organization dedicated to promoting bicycling, with the emphasis on bicycle racing, in the Greater New Orleans area. The NOBC was founded in 1968, and has remained at the forefront of competitive cycling activity since that time. The club is a member of USA Cycling, and actively promotes competitions throughout the year as part of the Louisiana-Mississippi Bicycle Racing Association.

The NOBC represents a wide range of cyclists, from beginning Juniors to seasoned Masters. NOBC members are always available to advise prospective members about training and racing techniques.

Club members organize training rides and seminars with the goal of developing riders for national competition. The club organizes group trips to area races, including the District Championships, and helps to defray team travel and entry fee expenses for club members who are USAC racing members of the NOBC. At the end of each season, there is the NOBC banquet, with awards for those members who were most successful or helpful during the year.

We invite you to become a member of this unique family of cyclists. All memberships are for the calendar year. All racing members should have the club jersey and/or skinsuit, available through the club. Jerseys are available to members at or below cost. Members are expected to wear the team jersey in all competitive events. USAC approved cycling helmets are required in all USAC competitions.

For more information, e-mail info@neworleansbicycleclub.org, or visit our Web site at www.neworleansbicycleclub.org/.

The Buffalo Bicycling Club has a jam-packed 2026 Season in store for our members!  By joining the Buffalo Bicycling Club, you will be treated to a full calendar of events every week from April through December.  The Buffalo Bicycling Club has many planned events, including:

  • 19 Sunday Series Club Training Races and Thursday Night Fireball Club Training Races
  • 2 USA Cycling Sanctioned Events (separate from membership, see calendar)
  • Sunday and weeknight group rides partnering with the NFBC (Niagara Frontier Bicycle Club) and the 716 Group Rides Wayland Brewing
  • Group Workouts led by our experienced club members
  • Cyclocross skills practices offered by Jon Siuta at the One O Four Farm

Click here to see our full calendar here on our website

 

 

MEMBERSHIP OPTION DETAILS

1. Full Membership: You'll receive access to all  group rides, Sunday Series races, _____ Night NFBC rides, Thursday Night Fireball criterium series, skills clinics, cyclocross clinics, and the end-of-year Banquet ride!

  • Note: Each Marshaling assignment completed gets your rewards!  Marshal a USAC Race or have a family/friend come marshal a Sunday Series Race and you get $40.  Marshal a Sunday Series Race yourself and you get 10 points towards that race!  See below!

2. Rookie Year Full Membership: Same as Full membership above. This option is for new riders who have never joined the Buffalo Bicycling Club before.  If this is your first year, the Buffalo Bicycling Club wants you to know we are excited you've decided to join us!  We were once new racers too, and we understand that figuring out what it all means can be nerve-racking.  Some of this may seem confusing, but we're here to help.  We want your first year of road racing with us to be a safe, fun, and educational experience.  We're looking forward to meeting you!  If you have any questions or concerns please don't hesitate to email us:

President: James Thompson,  president@buffalobicycling.com, jamestho1589@gmail.com

Women's Rider Rep: Erin Haskell, erinlhaskell@gmail.com 

Rider Development Director: Drew Scott, development@buffalobicycling.com, drscott2141@gmail.com

3. Rookie Full Membership plus Club Jersey: Same as Rookie Membership above for new members to the Buffalo Bicycling Club.  This membership will include a club Jersey from the Jakroo store below!  We want your first year with the Buffalo Bicycling Club to be a great, welcoming experience, and having a club jersey means you fit right in as a member of the club!  After registering, you will receive a one-time coupon code to order a jersey from the store in a separate email within 1 business day.  The extra cost in membership cost over a Rookie Membership means you get a new club jersey for half price- take advantage of the offer while it lasts!  This coupon applies to the Jakroo Nova 2.0 Race Jersey.  

4. Junior and College Student Membership: This is a FREE full membership for junior riders under 18 and registered college students.  Cycling and racing is a great sport to get into and we have a full range of group rides and club races to offer!  ***For new club members under 18, please contact or have parent/guardian contact club president James Thompson at jamestho1589@gmail.com or by hitting the “Contact Us" on this Bikereg website to discuss participation options.  Requiring a parent/guardian chaperone at events will be determined on an individual basis based on age, riding ability, and other factors.  

5. FREE Group Ride & Group Workout Membership: Access to all the Buffalo Bicycling Club Group Rides and Group Workouts Practices, Time Trials, and Skills Workshops.  A membership option for those looking to engage in our fun, social group rides and our mentorship program.  This will get you access to all Sunday and weeknight group rides where we partner with the NFBC (Niagara Frontier Bicycle Club) and the 716 Group Rides at Wayland Brewing.  This also gets you access to our new-for-2026 group workouts!  Come meet us at a workout led by one of our experienced members.  An example group workout would be riding out to a hill to do hill repeats at your own pace, and riding back to the start together. 

  • We are making this group ride/workout membership free as an easy entry point into the club to learn how to ride in a group and meet people.  If you want to be more involved and do our club races,  you can sign up for Full or Rookie Membership at any time as a mid-season upgrade.  

6. Cyclocross and Group Ride Membership: Access to our Cyclocross skills practices and clinics courtesy of Jon and Shannon Siuta at the One O Four Farm!  We value our partnership with them and the outreach to the cyclocross community as we host practices in the fall during CX season.  This also gets you access to the Group Rides and Group Workouts membership details above in #4. 

7. Out of Towner Membership: Anyone who lives outside of the 8 counties of WNY may purchase this membership to participate in club-hosted group rides and club races. Ideal for those just in town visiting or living in places nearby like Rochester or Ontario.

8. Booster Non-Membership: This is a great way to stay in touch with everything the club is offering through our emails, but for those who will not be participating in our group rides or club races.  This is not a membership option.  

NEED A MEMBERSHIP OPTION CHEAT SHEET?

 

MARSHALING

Marshals play a vital role in creating a safe and controlled environment for riders during events.  Marshaling responsibilities may vary from traffic management at a corner, driving a lead car during a sanctioned race, or helping with event setup/breakdown.  Please keep in mind that, without marshals, we cannot have races!  Thank you in advance for your participation and support. 

We need marshals to have our races happen, and we're prepared to offer you rewards! 

  • Marshal a USAC Race or have family/friends marshal the Sunday Series Club Races and you will be paid $40.  You can do this an unlimited number of times.
  • If you marshal a Sunday Series race yourself, we'll give you 10 points towards your Sunday Series Standings for that race!   For earning club points, you can do that a maximum of 2 times per season.  
  • We also need experienced riders to help mentor the B/C-group races for the Sunday Series.  Do that and you'll get 13 points towards your Sunday Series Standings for that race up to 1 time per season!

How to Sign Up to Marshaling Assignment:

When you purchase your membership, you will be prompted with a question to select a marshaling assignment. Select as many races as you'd like to marshal. 

If you'd like to sign up for additional marshaling assignments after purchasing your membership or can't make a commitment right now but want to sign up later, go to https://www.buffalobicyclingclub.com/marshal and select the event you would like to marshal.  We'll then provide you with additional instruction as the event nears.

 

Buffalo Bicycling Club KITS / APPAREL

Let's go Buff-a-lo! Represent the home team and look fresh doing it with brand new jerseys courtesy of Jakroo!

__________ 

More information on our website here: https://www.buffalobicyclingclub.com/shop/

 

Interested in even more racing?! Check out our USA Cycling sanctioned Races!  These are separate from club Membership, but open to anyone in the cycling community!  We get many out-of-town racers coming in for our sanctioned events to have highly competitive fields against the best from the northeast!

Sunday June 14th- Freedom Run Winery Road Race

Sunday July 12th- Grand Island Team Time Trial in Memory of Glenn Hansen and the New York State Team Time Trial Championships

 

The Fine Print:

Due to insurance and liability requirements, the Buffalo Bicycling Club requires all participants in training races, group rides, and club hosted events to be club members. 

1. The Buffalo Bicycling Club cannot allow "non-members" to participate in training races, rides, and events. You must purchase a Buffalo Bicycling Club membership from the options above. This approach will give members the option to select what best suits their availability and desired participation level.  The "Out of Town" option is not available to Buffalo-area residents regardless of desired participation level. 

2. All full membership options will give you full Buffalo Bicycling Club member rights per the club constitution and bylaws, but each will vary individually in event eligibility and marshaling requirements. 

3. As noted above, the Booster Non-Membership is not a membership and does not get you access to any club events, even though you will be on the emailing list.

Welcome to the VPCC Training Pass program! 

We’re excited to support your training journey at the Valley Preferred Cycling Center. Whether you’re gearing up for a full season or just getting started with a 30-Day Pass, your VPCC Training Pass is designed to make accessing track time simple, flexible, and rider-friendly.

Your VPCC Training Pass gives you unlimited access to VPCC training sessions during your active period, and it also ensures that both you and the velodrome are properly covered under USA Cycling’s insurance requirements. This protects everyone on the track and keeps our programs running safely and smoothly. A valid USA Cycling Membership + Race license enables insurance.

Once your pass is active, you’ll receive a unique coupon code that you’ll use when registering for training sessions on BikeReg. You can sign up for sessions one at a time or register for multiple dates in advance — whatever fits your training plan.

Below is a clear breakdown of how your pass works, what to expect, and how to get help if you need it.

VPCC Training Pass Policy

Pass Activation & Valid Dates

  • 30-Day Training Pass: 
    Begins on the next business day after purchase and stays active for 30 consecutive days.
  • Season Training Pass: 
    Begins on the next business day after purchase. Valid for the entire VPCC training season.
  • U19 Discounts: 
    Riders under 19 can purchase discounted 30-Day Passes and discounted Season Passes.

Your Unique Registration Code

Every rider receives a unique coupon code tied to their pass.
Use this code when registering for VPCC training sessions during your active pass period.

One Pass = One Rider

Each pass and coupon code is assigned to a single rider and cannot be shared or transferred.

Use Within Your Active Window

Registrations must fall within your pass’s valid dates.
Any session outside that window will be cancelled.

Need Help?

If your coupon code isn’t working or something doesn’t look right, VPCC Management is happy to help. Please use the event Contact Us form.

Responsible Use

Misuse of passes or codes may result in loss of pass privileges. Refunds are not provided in these cases.

VPCC Training Pass Program Overview

VPCC Training Passes—both 30-Day and Season—are issued through BikeReg as a unique coupon code that riders use to register for VPCC training sessions only on Bikereg.com and which are listed on the VPCC Track Schedule. You will need to register for each training session you wish to attend prior to that session.  If you already know your training dates, you can register for multiple sessions at a time and select the ‘register for another event’ option during checkout to add training dates for a different month.

Discounted pass options are available for U19 riders.

Single Session Training Fees

All VPCC training sessions have a $10 per-day, per-session fee, which covers required insurance and a small administrative surcharge. To register for a single session, please register for that date on bikereg.com event links listed above.

For 30-day or season pass holders, your coupon code applies automatically to your cart during registration as long as your pass is active.

Behind-the-Scenes Support

VPCC staff monitors Training Pass usage to ensure your code continues working throughout your valid period.

Join us for a great workouts developed and instructed by Coach Brian Lariviere. 

Live Dates

Every Monday Morning and Wednesday Evening 

Feel free to start early or join in a little late.

That time is not good for you?

We've got you covered!  Replay (join others at the same time) of each class will on that same day and the next days.

Can't make any of the live or replay classes?

No worries!  You'll have full access to the ON DEMAND classes where you can follow along and get the same great instruction on your own schedule.

These are NOT spin classes.  The programs are created for cyclists to maximized your progression throughout the season and get you ready for a great year of outdoor and indoor riding!

The Superior Cycling Association has built and maintains 34 miles of purpose built singletrack mountain bike trails in Cook County – including the Jackpot and High Climber trails, which connect Britton Peak trails to Lutsen Mountains. Join us for a focused 3-day block of structured Zwift training, live coaching, and online clinics designed to help you build fitness, sharpen your training approach, and start the next phase of your season with purpose.

Each morning runs from 9 a.m. to Noon (EDT), with plenty of interaction between CCNS coaches and fellow campers along the way. Expect hard work, useful feedback, and the kind of supportive group environment that makes training better.

What to Expect from vCamp

  • A pre-camp one-on-one goals review and power-profile analysis.
  • Three days of purposeful training designed to challenge your fitness and give us useful insight into your strengths and opportunities.
  • Live coaching, accountability, and the motivation of training alongside other committed athletes.
  • Informative clinics covering training, nutrition, race preparation, tactics, and performance.
  • Real-time coaching and tactical guidance during selected Zwift sessions.

Meet Your Coaches

Overview

Every athlete comes into camp with different goals, but each day follows a similar rhythm:

  • Riding starts at 9 a.m. EST
  • Pre-ride briefing covering the day's objectives, workout, route, and key coaching points.
  • Time on bike is generally 2.5-2.75 hours. Don't worry, we take breaks throughout to stretch and resupply!
  • Post-ride communication comes later in the day, featuring notable results and instructions for the next day.

CCNS vCamp Requirements

A few basic technical requirements help us make vCamp as interactive and useful as possible. Need assistance getting set up? We'll help you.

#1: vCamp athletes must be able to communicate through Zoom during the training window.

#2: You must have access to a browser or secondary device separate from your Zwift display for clinics, presentations, and other camp content.

#3: Daily attendance matters. vCamp is designed as a complete 3-day training block, and the value comes from participating consistently from day to day. Please plan to be ready and online before each day's scheduled start.

Your First Steps

Step 1: Register for the vCamp that fits your schedule. December's vCamp is here

Step 2: If you are not a current CCNS athlete, schedule your pre-camp call with a CCNS coach so we can review your riding, goals, and current fitness.

That's it! 
You're on your way to three productive days of riding, learning, and building momentum for the season ahead.

Want to Learn More?

Wondering what the daily training will look like or which clinic topics we'll cover?
Email us at vCamp@charlescoaching.com for a detailed camp overview and answers to any questions you may have.

EventName: Bill Bauer Memorial Exhibition Roller Races at Brands Cycle
EventNotes:
Check in and day-of registration will open at 5:30pm and qualifying will begin at 6:00pm
 
The rollers races are traditionally run using TRACK bikes but we have and will continue to allow road bikes.
 
All bikes will be "ROLLED OUT" with the maximum distance that the bike can travel with rotation of the cranks being 303 inches/ This equates to a gearing of 96.4, usually achieved with a 50 or 51 chainring and a 14 cog on the rear depending on the size of the rear tire.
 
All entrants will ride a 10 lap (1 mile) Time trial which will determine seeding.
 
The top 8 will Advance
Time permitting, Anyone outside the top 8 will be allowed to ride a 2nd ride to determine overall places outside the top 8
 
The top 8 will race match races as follows:
Heat 1 1st vs 8th
Heat 2 2nd vs 7th
Heat 3 3rd vs 6th 
Heat 4 4th vs 5th
 
Riders will advance to 1/4 finals as follows:
1/4 #1 Loser heat 1 vs loser heat 4 
1/4 #2 Loser heat 2 vs loser heat 3
1/4 #3 Winner heat 1 vs winner heat 4
1/4 #4 Winner heat 2 vs winner heat 3
 
Riders advance as follows: 
Loser 1/4 # 1 vs 1/4 # 2 for 7th and 8th places overall
Loser 1/4 # 3 vs Loser 1/4 # 4 for 5th and 6th places
Winner 1/4 # 1 vs Winner 1/4 # 2 advance to Semi Finals
Winner 1/4 # 3 vs Winner 1/4 # 4 advance to Semi Finals
 
Riders Advance as follows
Losers of above Semi Finals advance to Final for 3rd and 4th place overall.
Winners of above Semi Final advance to final for 1st and 2nd place overall.
PresentedBy: GBSC/LIWA and Brands Cycle and Fitness
