EventNotes:
Event Day Timeline

SATURDAY START TIMES & EVENT TIMELINE:

  • 48 Mile Ride - 8:00 AM Start
  • 48 Mile Ride - 8:30 AM Start
  • 32 Mile Ride - 9:00 AM Start
  • 32 Mile Ride - 9:30 AM Start
  • 15 Mile Ride - 10:00 AM Start
  • After Party Begins - 11:00 AM (beer service starts)
  • Raffle Drawing - 1:15 PM
  • END OF EVENT - 2:00 PM (beer service ends)

 

WHY ARE THERE DIFFERENT START TIMES:

We have multiple start times for each distance (besides the 15-mile ride), for a few reasons

  • Provide registrants the flexibility to take either the early or late start time for each distance.
  • Space riders out on course, so we do not interfere too heavily in local, regular traffic patterns.
  • Stay within capacity limitations for the brewery space, as well as local and municipal requirements.
  • Finally, give our staff and volunteers the ability to check in riders in a timely fashion and not get overrun with too many participants at once. 

 

MORNING ARRIVAL:

  • Please arrive 30 minutes before your designated start time to allow for plenty of time to park and check in. Check your confirmation email or log in to your account HERE to see which distance and start time you selected.
  • For capacity and permitting reasons, we check in one start time at a time. If you are more than a half-hour early to the check-in tent, you will not be checked in until the next ride goes off. We appreciate your patience with our volunteers. As you wait, please enjoy some morning snacks, pastries, and hot coffee.
  • Limited Capacity Event - Please arrive planning to ride in the event time slot that you registered for. We have time slots for many reasons, including safety, permitting, and other capacity considerations.

 

DO NOT FORGET:

  • HYDRATION STARTS IN THE DAYS LEADING UP TO EVENT DAY
  • PHOTO ID (bring with you in the morning for registration)
  • Must wear a HELMET to ride
  • Water bottle for hydration (We'll have plenty of water for refilling in the morning, rest stops, and post-ride)
  • Sunscreen
  • Bright colored clothing for maximum visibility
  • Change of shoes/clothes for the post-ride party
  • Feel free to bring lawn/beach chairs for guaranteed seating in the post-ride party
  • CASH or CREDIT CARD for post-ride merch! Our shirts are really fun! You won't want to miss out!
  • If you want guaranteed seating in the post-ride party, feel free to bring a beach/lawn chair.
  • No bike trailers or children under the age of 16 are permitted to ride in this event
  • This event is a private party closed to the public. If you have friends & family coming to the post-ride party, please inform them to buy a post-ride entry ticket.

 

MORNING CHECK-IN:
 

  • PHOTO ID required to check in.
  • There will be multiple lines to check in/register.
  • At check-in, you'll be given a wristband and bike plate with a unique number for photographer identification. We'll have (3) professional photographers taking photos throughout the event. Your bike plate number is how you'll find these photos later! Please secure the bike plate to the front of your bike with the zip ties given to you (SEE EXAMPLE IMAGE BELOW).
    • Bike plate is mandatory, mounted to the handlebar or head tube, so course marshals, photographers, and volunteers can distinguish participants.
    • Your event photos will be available for purchase on the Monday after the event. KEEP YOUR BIKE PLATE so you have the number to identify your photos with our partnering photography company.
  • Complimentary Pastries, Snacks, and COFFEE while you wait for your ride to begin.
  • Questions about the route? Make your way to our route information tent for a physical cue sheet and instructions on how to download the turn-by-turn route instructions on the Ride With GPS app.

 

THE RIDE:

SAVE THE SAG SUPPORT PHONE NUMBER WILL BE GIVEN TO YOU IN PRE-RIDE EMAILS.

  • We'll begin the rides in half-hour intervals (the start time you registered for). In addition to the Ride with GPS turn-by-turn instructions, all routes are marked on the pavement.
    • Route markings on the road are color-coordinated depending on which distance you're riding. The ride director will explain the route arrows before each ride goes off!
       
      • 15, 32, and 48-mile rides generally have rest stops unless otherwise stated in pre-ride emails.
      • RSVP to the event on the Ride With GPS app for the rest stop locations.
      • A few bike pumps, as well as a basic patch kit and small tools, will be available for small fixes. If you have a larger issue, please contact SAG support. The rest stop will also have a medical kit (for non-serious injuries) and portable toilets for participants to use.
      • This is your reminder to bring any extra tubes or repair kits for your bike. Sometimes the SAG wagon will not have your specific tube size, so it's good to bring your own if you have it!
  • Each ride's start time and distance are designed so that the average rider's pace returns to the brewery post-ride party from 11:30 - 12:30 PM. There is no time limit. It is ok if you come back later; just be aware that the charity raffle drawing is at 1:15 PM. If you finish after 1:15 PM, we are sorry, but we cannot hold up the raffle drawing any longer due to a large majority of riders already finishing and waiting.

 

About SAG/Mechanical Support and What to Expect:

Pre-Ride Support

After checking in, visit the SUPPORTING BIKE SHOP teams at their tent in the event space for quick, pre-ride mechanical checks. They can help with minor issues like lubing your chain, making small adjustments, and performing safety checks.

Please do not expect them to provide time-consuming or expensive services like providing or installing new bike parts. We recommend taking care of any major maintenance needs before event day by visiting shops like Stone Harbor Bike & Beach Shop in advance. The on-site mechanics will need to work quickly to help as many riders as possible before the start of each ride.

During the Ride

  • For a mechanical issue: If you have a bike issue during the ride, text the SAG SUPPORT phone number your location & issue. The SAG team will do their best to get you back on the road. For the best chance of success, remember to bring your own spare parts, tubes, and tools.

  • For a medical emergency: IMMEDIATELY CALL 911. The SAG team is not equipped to handle medical emergencies.

  • Physical limitations: SAG support is prioritized for mechanical issues. While we will do our best to help, we cannot guarantee transportation back to the brewery for riders who cannot finish due to physical limitations. If you have a serious medical issue, you should call for an ambulance. 

  • Please be smart: Know your limits, and prepare appropriately by hydrating in the days leading up to the event and checking your bike for safety issues before arriving.

 

AFTER PARTY:
 

  • The FINISH LINE is in the same place as the ride started. Arrive back under the Bikes & Beers banner and be ready to pose for your best FINISHING PHOTO!
    • Then, please make way for the riders finishing behind you.
  • We will have bike parking at the brewery. However, if you drove to the event and parked close, please rack your bike back on your vehicle to create as much space in the event area as possible.
  • After arriving back at the brewery, use the tab attached to your wristband to pick up your pint glass under the Bikes & Beers tent. You'll see signage stating "PINT GLASS PICK-UP"
  • Also attached to your wristband are tabs to redeem (2) REWARDING BEERS!
    • The host brewery will have beer redemption tents set up in the event space!
    • The host brewery will have some non-alcoholic options available in its taprooms. Also, check the Bikes & Beers merchandise tent for some additional options.
  • Don't forget to bring your wallet for post-ride food offered by multiple food trucks.
  • If you arrive back at the brewery before the after-party is set up for beer service, please be patient. We will be working as fast as we can to change over the event from registration to the post-ride party! The after-party officially begins @ 11:00 AM.

 

PRIZE RAFFLE:
 

  • Every participant gets (1) raffle ticket included in their pint glass. FOR MORE CHANCES TO WIN, more tickets are available for purchase, with proceeds benefiting our charity partners. The raffle will be drawn at 1:15 PM. You have to be present to win the raffle prizes, including A NEW BEACH CRUISER (Valued at $500+), 4 FREE B&B RIDES, BREWERY GEAR, CAR BIKE RACK, BIKE LIGHTS, BIKE LOCK, SPONSOR GIVEAWAYS, and much more!
    • Why is the Raffle at 1:15 PM? Some riders finish early, and some riders finish later. 1:15 PM is the sweet spot for almost all riders to have a chance to finish and enjoy the post-ride party before raffle time. If you finish very early and do not want to stick around for the raffle, please also understand that there are a few riders who finish late and might miss the raffle. With the experience of over a hundred events, we do our best to accommodate the large majority of riders who want the raffle drawing at 1:15 PM. 

 

MERCHANDISE TENT:

  • T-shirts, jerseys, shorts, tanks, hats, socks, etc. will be available for purchase at the post-ride party.
  • We have a credit card reader, but as a small business, we prefer cash purchases for the speed/cost of transactions. There is a $25 minimum for credit card purchases. Please remember to bring cash.
  • Commemorate the ride and celebrate your accomplishments with one of our fun t-shirts or cycling jerseys!

 

PRE-ORDER MERCHANDISE:

  1. Pick up your pre-ordered merchandise at the event after-party at our merchandise tent! You can check to see if you have pre-ordered merch by logging into your account.

Everything else will be sent to you in pre-ride information emails. If you have any questions in the meantime, please reach us at info@bikesandbeers.com

EventNotes:
This is one big delicious cookie crusher and a rider favorite!  Just north of Austin, we've found the most amazing gravel on your choice of 16, 34, 46, and 61 mile options.  There is a great mix of chunky, smooth, and sandy gravel, with a couple of beautiful paved sections for the 34, 46, and 61, and loads of tree covered canopies along the route.  There are plenty of rolling hills and beautiful scenery for gravel cruisers and even the most serious racer types!

We'll be waiting for you at the finish line celebration at the Milano Civic Center with lunch and drinks benifiting the Milam Touch of Love animal welfare group!

 

Registration closes the Thursday night before the event, and all registered participants will recieve an information email with all the needed facts and GPS files.  All riders should start the ride with a minimum of 2 water bottles or a hydration pack, all needed nutrition, and a repair kit for flat tires and minor mechanical needs.  Riders should also carry a cell phone for emergency calls, and have the gps files loaded onto their bike computer or phone in the Ride With GPS app for navigation.  The routes are not marked.

 

Please see our website and facebook page for more info!  www.capitalcityracingtexas.com  www.facebook.com/capitalcityracingtexas.com/  www.instagram.com/capitalcityracingtexas/

 

See you out there in Milano, TX!

Safety Cutoff Times: For the 35- and 50-mile courses, each racer must pass these cutoff times or ride in the safety vehicle back to the venue.  This ensures each rider completes the course within the allotted time and safely.  These times may change slightly based on final course routing.
  • Lower Sunset Parking Lot Aide Station (mile 13) - 1:00 pm
  • Northwest Access Road (mile 23) - 2:30 pm (north end of Lower Foothills)
  • If riding the 50-mile race - Roundhouse (mile 35) - 2:30 pm
Category Consolidation: Race director may combine race categories if there are not enough registrations to support each category.  We do not combine Male / Female categories.
Course Pre-riding: 99% of the El Paso Puzzler Course is within the Franklin Mountain State Park.  Your race day entry to the park is included in your registration.  If you ride the course on any other day, you must obtain a day-use permit ($5 per day, per user).  Those permits can be obtained at the Iron Rangers (self-pay stations) at any one of these trailheads (Lost Cow, Roundhouse, or Chuck Heinrich Park), the park visitor center at the Tom Mays unit,  or online at  https://texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com/camping/franklin-mountains-state-park/r/deDetails.do?contractCode=TX&parkId=1200020
Merchandise: All merchandise purchased online will be available for pickup at packet pickup times or the BMBA tent during the event.  No shipping will be offered, and any merchandise or packets not picked up within 30 days of the race will be considered a donation to the BMBA and used appropriately.
Parking: Parking is limited at the venue and will be first come, first served.  Carpooling is highly recommended. $5 donation.
Spectators: All spectators entering the Franklin Mountain State Park will be required to pay the daily usage fee.  That can be paid via the Iron Rangers (self-pay stations at the trailheads) or online at Here.  If you pay online, please print the permit and keep it on your dashboard.
Camping: Primitive camping will be open at the venue starting Friday at 1 pm and closing Monday at 10 am.
E-Bikes: This is an endurance race, so no form of e-bikes is allowed.  Any rider who shows up with an e-bike will be disqualified and not permitted to race even in a noncompetitive manner.  There will be no refunds for disqualified riders.
Weather: Although the weather in El Paso is usually amazing in January, there is always the chance of race delays or cancellations due to weather.  We will do our best to hold the race on the dates scheduled.  If there is a weather event that does not allow for a safe race on Saturday or Sunday, the race will be moved to Monday.  If the race is canceled due to weather, there will be no refunds as this is a not-for-profit fundraiser.
No refunds for individual cancellations: If there is a risk that you may not be able to attend, we highly suggest you look into BikeReg Refund Protection, which can be purchased during checkout.  Make sure you review the details before purchase to see what cancellations are covered.  BikeReg does offer individual participant cancellation insurance if purchased during registration; see here for details: https://www.bikereg.com/knowledge-base/104/Participant-Registration-Insurance--Allianz-Registration-Protection
 
All proceeds from the Puzzler support the Borderland Mountain Bike Association-, a not-for-profit run by volunteers.  We support our mountain and trail system with every dollar raised!

Welcome back to the L.A. Tourist Race series for 2027!  If you have never done an L.A. Tourist event here's what you need to know. 

 You will be given 4 check points, given out the week of the race, that you will use to make your map.  At each checkpoint you will find a book, at that book tear out your corresponding race number and move on.  First one back with the correct numbered pages Wins! 

 

 

The basic tenants of the event to which all participants must adhere:

  1. Be fully self supported. Do not pre-stash or have others shuttle your food, water, tools or supplies while on the route. Plan accordingly.
  2. Know how to fix your stuff. No one will be sweeping the course. You need to be able to figure out your own extraction, if needed.
  3. Respect the course. Leave no trace ethos in place. Leave only tire tracks and footprints.
  4. Respect others. Other participants. Hikers. Equestrians. Forest Service.
  5. Like in years past, your participant number is the page you must grab at the check point from the book at that location. Wrong page or no page will equal "no check point".
  6. When on public and forst service roads, follow the rules of the road.
  7. Know how to navigate from point to point during the event. Never rely on others to be your naviagation.
  8. First aid and hydration are important. Prepare your own water and food or plan your food and water stops ahead of time.  

These races happen Rain or Shine, we do not cancel or postpone due to rain or snow.  These events can take you from sea level to over the 5k feet of elevation.  You may ride thru snow or cross streams and rivers so prepare yourself and keep an eye on the weather as event day approaches.  All registration sales are final

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics/JUMP Essentials & ADV JUMP Technique : Phoenix/Gilbert Jan 23
EventNotes:
Are YOU ready to invest in your riding? Be safer, more confident, have more fun because you KNOW what needs to happen on the trail and you're familiar with how to execute. This session isn't for everyone, we're quite ok admitting that. This is for riders that are ready to be in a setting with coaches that actually have relevant experience in doing AND teaching the subject matter. We GUARANTEE you'll leave this session with the tools needed to become the rider you've always wanted to be. 

Founders and Lead Coaches Rob and Rich Drew will break down all of the nuance behind success when jumping. From groomed takeoffs to janky rock kickers, the brothers will provide deep insight into what needs to happen, how it needs to happen, and when! 

 

JUMP Essentials Session:

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get plenty of reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
 

ADVANCED JUMP TECHNIQUES: 
Are you ready to take your jumping to the next level? This is the session to make it happen! Refinement is the key here and breaking it down deeper with bigger jumps and more in depth video analysis is the way to make it happen. 

RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

Welcome to Marty's Ride Club! 

The MRC is committed to helping our members enjoy the sport of cycling at the highest level. 

Become a member today and enjoy the following benefits: 

1. Group rides led by the the best ride leaders in the NJ cycling community. Collectively, our ride leaders have over 50 years of experience in leading rides, and they know all of the best routes in the area.

2. Access to Ride with GPS Club account. Get the app and take advantage of the paid features unlocked for all routes in the club library. You can also download maps to your phone to use offline, saving battery and eliminating data usage. Members can also export TCX files of club routes with advanced turn notifications on their GPS units, or print branded, customized PDF maps and cue sheets.

3. Members also get access to club accounts for Strava, and Zwift!  In addition, you will be invited to join our private FB group for up to the minute information on rides and events.

4. MRC provides exclusive discounts on select Trek Travel Vacations.

5. Marty's Reliable Cycle will offer exclusive monthly discounts for club members on select products and services. These discounts alone will easily cover the membership fee.

6. Early access to special events.

7.  Ride in style wearing our signature blue color and get discounted club price on your next Marty's kit!  

8. Mountain bike rides led by seasoned riders who know the local parks like the back of their hands!

9. The club will also host many of the events you've come to love over the years, such as:  Gravel Events, The Lewis Morris Challenge, Iron Mountain Enduro, Dickerson Mine Endurance, The Turkey Fry Ride, and many more to come!

As the club grows and evolves, so will the above list of events and activities. We have much in store for the future including bike packing trips, road, gravel, mountain bike destination weekend trips, a trip up to Vermont to ride The Kingdom Trails, and maybe one day we will even bring the MRC abroad. When you are busy "Saving The World with Bikes", the possibilities are endless. We can't wait for you to Join The Ride! 

Marty’s Ride Club (MRC) was founded with the mission of bringing cyclists together to enjoy the sport of cycling. When you join the MRC you’re joining a community of like-minded people who are passionate about the sport of cycling. We provide a welcoming, friendly and safe environment for members of all levels to pursue their health and fitness goals. By joining the MRC you can truly experience the most fun on two wheels! You’ll find that club membership opens up a new community where you can make new friends, learn from more experienced riders, share routes, training tips, and create a new social group. So don’t wait, be a part of the MRC, and join the ride!

 

 Once you have joined MRC you will immediately receive a welcome email with important club information as well as a link to MRC Ride With GPS Club.  Please read this email in its entirety as it contains important links and rider safety information.  Membership is for the calendar year.  Membership does not auto-renew.

Featuring a 36 Mile point to point course, the Prickly Pedal starts in Cave Creek in front of the Flat Tire Bike Shop, 6032 E Cave Creek Rd, Cave Creek, AZ 85331, and rides up through town to Spur Cross where you’ll join the Maricopa Trail all the way over to the finish line at Lake Pleasant Regional Park’s 10 Lane Boat Ramp. The event showcases the diversity of the Maricopa Trail and supports the Maricopa Trail and Park Foundation. Aggressive ascents and descents, grinding it out on the flats, rocks, water, sand, mud, and roller coaster runs are all part of the fun of this challenging course.

Besides being a challenging, exciting, fun race, why does the Prickly Pedal exist? To pour every dollar of race revenue into efforts that will add more pristine miles of Maricopa Trail for riders to enjoy. MT+PF envisions this event evolving into a world class, multi-day, endurance stage mountain bike race, drawing thousands of fans to the desert southwest.

The ride features numerous short, steep, rocky climbs and descents…some of which will require you to dismount and hike. This is not a race for the inexperienced – finish times for most racers are estimated at 3-4 hours. Be prepared for a long day in the saddle. This is a tough mountain bike race. 

Camping at Lake Pleasant

We have reserved two of the group camping sites just down the road from the finish line at Lane 10 Boat Ramp. Camping info is below.

No hook ups for Rv’s, however RV’s are welcome in the area. (Dump station is across the way). Tents and vehicle camping is ok.

Individual fires will not be allowed, there is a large fire pit by the ramada’s for use. (unless we are in a fire ban).

Water and 110 amp electricity is available, however is shared (these are located at the picnic ramada’s).

Flushable Restrooms and Showers are located in both areas, however will be shared with all group campers, including the 3rd group site which is not our racers.

There will be limited distance between campers, this will be based on the total number of campers. We do have a overflow area also reserved should we reach capacity.

We will assign camping spaces based on how many and what type of units make reservations. We will communicate these assignments during race week.

Camping Fee is $22.00 per night per unit. (A unit is whatever is used to sleep in, this would include a sleeping bag on the ground, tent, vehicle or RV). You can purchase a camping space on the merchandise page.

EventNotes:
The Next Wild Chapter - Women’s Winter Retreat: 

A weekend for active women in midlife to pause, listen, and explore what’s next

Ride, Hike, Move, Reset, Refresh, Restore

Presented by Basecamp Kitten + Sacred Trees Retreats

Date: February 5-7, 2027 
Location: Basecamp Frederick Lodge - 9106 Hamburg Rd, Frederick, MD
Contacts: Alex Forte Howell (Basecamp Frederick/Dirty Kitten) & Anne Cochrane (Sacred Trees Retreats)
 
Winter invites us to slow down, turn inward, and listen. This weekend retreat is designed for active women in midlife to reconnect with their changing bodies, explore what they want from the next phase, spend time in nature, and experience the power of community. Through workshops, storytelling, journaling, movement, small group activities, shared meals, and fireside conversations, we’ll honor the stories that have shaped us—and begin imagining the stories we want to write next.

About the Ride

Tour de Palm Springs in Coachella Valley is an event designed to raise money for nonprofit organizations in the Coachella Valley. Each year the organizers endeavor to support almost 100 local charities with money raised. 

Palm Springs beautiful weather, gorgeous mountain scenery and thousands of bike riders make the Tour de Palm Springs a fundraising event like no other!

Event Information

Vendor Expo: February 5 and February 6, 2027 - South Palm Canyon Drive

While we've rarely had to enforce race rules at our events, having clear guidelines in place is important to ensure fairness and consistency should any issues arise during a race.

Our events are not sanctioned by USA Cycling (USAC), but we use their rules as a general guideline, recognizing USAC as the national governing body for cycling in the Unites States.  As a grassroots race organization, we understand that some USAC rules may not apply to the nature or format of our events.  The Race Director reserves the right to make final decisions on situations not specifically addressed by USAC rules or when adjustments are necessary to best fit our events.

The Dansville Dangler is the first gravel endurance event of the SSIC Gravel Series in Steuben County. Think of it as an early spring kick in the ass! The course consists of primarily gravel/dirt/seasonal roads with paved connectors. Youll be on a 16 mile Dirt Time Trial! The course will be open and traffic will be on the roads, so please obey all traffic signs and rules of the road. There are some steep downhills and some challenging uphills. Be prepared to come to a complete stop for any traffic. You will be timed over a 15 mile course with 1600'. 

Please reach out with any questions you may have. Gravel bikes recommended. Mountain bikes are capable. NO ROAD BIKES.

2nd Annual 

FRANZ WEBER MEMORIAL RIDE

Sunday, April 18, 2027

In April 2025 we lost our Club President, a great public servant, friend, and anchor of our community. Franz served the Hawaii Cycling Club and the entire Big Island community selflessly, generously, transparently, energetically, and unconditionally. We hold Franz in our permanent memory for his high ethical conduct, unwavering dedication to helping others, positive attitude, and endless energy and availability, especially to those in greatest need. Franz embodied all the virtues of a dedicated champion for the community and as an enduring model of generosity and kindness.

Join the Big Island cycling community in honoring Franz for this annual recreational group ride following Franz's favorite route from the Kona Community Aquatic Center to the Queen's Shops at Waikoloa. Riders have the option of a 24.5-mile one way ride or 49-mile round trip. Hospitality Coffee and Refreshments will be available in the parking lot behind Bike Works Beach & Sports at the Waikoloa Queens Shops. This event is intended for cyclists of all abilities and age levels who enjoy a reasonable level of cycling fitness. Ride whatever bike you prefer.

Disclosure: This is a non-sanctioned event. Participation in this event is AT YOUR OWN RISK. You are responsible for your own safety. A properly secured helmet is required at all times while riding
 

All participants will be asked to sign a liability waiver before the ride

EventNotes:
The RELIANCE Deep Woods Gravel Grinder is a full weekend of grassroots gravel grinding in the Cherokee National Forest east of Chattanooga, TN, April 23-25! 

THE RACES
RELIANCE offers two race routes on Saturday (70 miles/8100 ft of climbing and 46 miles/5600 ft of climbing) and one race route on Sunday (28 miles/3700 ft of climbing). All three race routes will have separate podiums for all categories.

THE RIDES
RELIANCE also offers a relaxed 13-mile shakeout ride on Friday, along with challenging recreational routes of 24 miles on Saturday and 26 miles on Sunday. All routes will be timed and all two-day finishers will receive a finisher medal!

Plus
Music, Prizes, Food, Beer & Camping!

What to Expect: 

  • Amazing Scenery
  • Grassroots Camaraderie
  • Good Food & Tasty Beer!

What NOT to Expect: 

  • Flat Roads
  • Easy Routes
  • Champagne Gravel

Saturday Routes:

  • 25 miles, 2900 feet of climbing, 70% gravel
  • 46 miles, 5600 feet of climbing, 50% gravel (race route)
  • 70 miles, 8100 feet of climbing, 60% gravel (race route)

Sunday Routes:

  • 26 miles, 2900 feet of climbing, 60% gravel
  • 28 miles, 3700 feet of climbing, 70% gravel (race route)

All routes will be timed, and Prizes & Awards will be presented to the top 3 in each race category both Saturday and Sunday.

All riders will have access to well stocked aid stations on the routes and will enjoy post-ride food, beer, live music and festivities both Saturday and Sunday after the rides! Free swag like water bottles, pint glasses, bandanas and koozies are included in the price, and we'll also have plenty of Tennessee Gravel merch available both days!

We are SOLD OUT of the reservable campsites at our homebase at Hiwassee Outfitters. However, free camping will be available nearby on a first-come first-served basis. For all of the available camping options, please see tennesseegravel.com/reliance-camping.

The Open Range Gravel Race is an ultra-endurance bicycle race through a remote and rugged area of the state.  Start time for the 200k race is 8am and there will be a 10 MPH pace cutoff.  The distance for the 200k will be between 125 - 132 miles. If you don't think you can maintain a 10 mph average, please feel free to sign up for the 100k+ or the 50ish.  The 100k+ starts at 8:30am.  The 50ish starts at 9am

Pratt Volunteer Fire Department will handle Drop Bag and rider extraction service. If you want a drop bag delivered and returned, sign up for their service.  Proceeds go to support the Pratt Volunteer Fire Department.   

Sun City and Medicine Lodge will be the checkpoints for the race.  Sun City is around 35 mile mark and Medicine Lodge will be around mile 80.  Checkpoints will have water and light snacks.  There is a drop bag service available (proceeds support Pratt Volunteer Fire) to riders. Bring your nutrition in a clearly marked bag or soft-sided cooler and we'll move it to the checkpoint(s).  Heavy duty slider zip bags with ducktape and name work great!  If racing in the 200k they will take 2 bags (one for Sun City, one for Medicine Lodge- they will not move the same bag from checkpoint to checkpoint). 

The 50ish will be close to 50k (31 miles) this year and still get riders on a loop of private ranch lands.  There is no checkpoint on this route. 

While we do allow transfers up to registration close, we do not allow refunds for race fee.  If you think you might need a refund, we suggest the race insurance provided through BikeReg.  Proceeds from Open Range go to local non-profit.

The 100 Kilometer (63 mi.); 65 Kilometer (40 mi.); and 35 Kilometer (22 mi.) course is pedaled over paved roads in this beautiful and scenic North Texas area. It is a fast and challenging course. Be prepared for some long and steep climbs up rolling hills and the exhilaration you'll experience coming down!

ENTRY FEES: All entries postmarked by April 19TH, 2027, will be $50 per rider. All entries postmarked after April 19TH, 2027, and those who register the day of the ride will be $60 per rider. Registration and packet pick up will be on Friday from 9am-6pm @ the Sacred Heart Community Center - 706 North Main Street. On Saturday packet pick-up & day of registration will be from 7am-8:30am at Heritage Hall at 1902 Weber Ranch Rd., Muenster, Texas.

Please join us for refreshments at the Finish Area located on the South East corner of Heritage Park!  Free admission into GermanFest held at Heritage, which includes 2 FREE cold beers from the Muenster Jaycees trailer! You may purchase an event t-shirt for $10 as an add on when you register.

RAIN OR SHINE: There will be a ride and there will be no refunds. Rally begins at 9 AM! 

All proceeds from this event will benefit education for Sacred Heart Catholic School.

EventNotes:
You aren't going to want to miss the 4th annual Coal Country Roubaix!  This gravel/dirt road ride will test your ability. Each course is filled with challenging climbs, lots of gravel, some technical downhills, minimal pavement, potentially mud and who knows maybe even snow!  

For 2027, there are FOUR route options - 35 miler, 100k, 100 mile & 300 miler. ALL routes are roughly 75% gravel roads! And, lots & lots of elevation! If you're looking for a challenging course, this is your event! Oh & did we mention the routes are in REVERSE this year?! 

The 2027 routes will be posted soon!

About The Ride:

All routes are scenic tours through back country roads with excellent views! These roads are great for riding. Little traffic, little maintenance & lots of fun! You never know what to expect, it all depends on the weather! Could be dry & fast. Could’ve just be a total mud fest. Either way, you don’t want to miss it!

Cyclocross, Mountain, Single-Speed, Fixed gear, Fat bikes, E-bikes and tandem bicycles are welcomed & encouraged!

We will have a mass/neutral start at 9AM sharp with a police rolling escort through town. The course will NOT be marked prior to the event, gps routes maps are available for download. You are responsible for your own navigation. The course will NOT be closed to traffic. Cycling rules of the road apply, i.e. stop at all stop signs, yield to cars, no more than 2 riders abreast and do not cross yellow center line. Please do not litter. A sag vehicle will be on course to help out if needed or in case of any emergencies.

Timing and results provided by Ronin Race Timing! Live results here: http://Roninresults.com/coal

EventNotes:
The Bryce River Foundation is named in memory of Bryce River Waldrop, who we lost May 31, 2023.  The Foundation exists to come alongside mental health professionals and organizations who are providing suicide prevention training and education as well as good mental health practices and advocacy to end the stigma of mental health care.  

River fostered a love of cycling and bike repair so hosting a bike ride seemed to make a lot of sense.  Cycling was a coping mechanism for his depression, and it served him well over the years.  Exercise has also been proven to be beneficial to your mental health.

All proceeds will benefit the Bryce River Foundation and our mission to reduce and prevent suicide.

The ride features three routes:  a 7-mile Family Ride, a 27-mile intermediate route, and a 50-mile advanced route.  The 50-mile route will have an option to be shortened if a cutoff time is not met (more details in registration).  There are also registration options for folks who wish to support the event but don't care to ride ("Please Don't Make Me Ride!").  

For the 2nd year in a row, we are adding a 3-mile ruck.

This event will also have things for the whole family including a pop-up vendor market, fun jumps, and more.  Please join us as we Ride Towards Tomorrow!

Dirty Kitten Gralley Cat MMXXVII

"Where Gravel Meets Adventure"

April 24, 2027 @ Locust Hill Farm & Preserve - Rapidan, VA

Presented by Dirty Kitten Productions

 

So...What’s a “Gralley Cat”? 

Gravel + Alleycat + Adventure 

An “alleycat” is an unsanctioned, informal, underground bike race that traditionally takes place in cities and urban areas where participants race from one checkpoint to the next in an effort to complete all challenges and/or hit as many locations as possible. Think: Adventure Scavenger Hunt!

The Dirty Kitten Gralley Cat (DKGC) is a “choose-your-own-adventure” alley-cat style bike/run event on the grounds of Locust Hill Farm & Preserve (LHFP) in Rapidan, VA. Instead of following a set course from start to finish, participants are able to select their own route as they make their way around the property, visiting multiple checkpoints along the way. Both competitive & recreational participants are welcome. 

Participants have the choice of doing either a “short course” (~20 miles) or “long course" (~40 miles) individually, in pairs, or as small teams (runners can do anywhere from 5-20 miles). All participants are given a map of the course during check-in the morning of the event on which the checkpoints, course boundaries, and key navigational points are clearly marked. After visiting all designated checkpoints, participants return to the start area where their scorecards are verified and finish times recorded. 

NOTE: There is not a GPS route or map available for this event. Participants receive a paper or digital map of the course the morning of the event (no, you can't get a course map sooner so don't ask!)

Why Gralley Cat?

  • We think it’s cool, unique, and sounds fun!
  • It’s a good way to have a competitive event without a traditional mass start
  • This format gives us a chance to showcase different areas of the farm.
  • There are roads on LHFP that don’t really work in a traditional race format: Nobody wants to be chugging along in a group only to slam on their brakes and pull a 180 for an out-and-back during a race.
  • It can be as competitive or non-competitive as you make it. Want to plot the most efficient route and ride your heart out to get the fastest time? That’s cool. Want to tour the property and just have fun? That’s awesome, too! 

Categories: Solo, Duo, Team, Juniors* 

  • Solo - 1 participant (all levels)
  • Duo - 2 participants (all levels)
  • Team - 3, 4, or 5 participants (all levels)
  • Junior - participants under the age of 18

*We have both ride & run options. Run participants "choose their own adventure" and can cover anywhere up to 20 miles if they wish. The run course will be an abbreviated version of the ride course with run-specific checkpoints.

Registration: Reg opens January 2027 - fees increase on Feb 15th and April 1st

NOTE: Duo & Team participants must enter additional member names at registration

  • NEW "Purrathlon" (short run + ride): starting at $70 PER PERSON
  • Long Purrito (~40 miles): starting at $60 PER PERSON
  • Short Purrito (~20 miles): starting at $50 PER PERSON
  • Run (5-20 miles): starting at $30 PER PERSON
  • Juniors $5-10 OFF registration

*Day-of registration will be available 8-11am on site. An additional $5 fee will be added. 

Refunds & Transfers: 

There are NO refunds for this event. Transfers are available upon request (once the event is sold out). If the event must be canceled due to health, safety, or severe weather conditions, participants will receive a BikeReg credit equal to the FULL amount of their registration fee (not including any service fees) along with additional charges for merchandise, food, etc to be used toward another Dirty Kitten Productions event.

Rules: Participants are expected to follow all event rules & guidelines stated below 

HELMETS REQUIRED! NO AEROBARS!! 

Participants are asked to arrive at least 30 minutes before their designated start time, check in with a staff member at registration (cabin), warm up only in designated areas (not on course), be prepared when called to the starting area (all duo and team members must be present), and check-out at the finish when their ride/run is complete.

The course will be marked at turns and intersections. Some sections of the property will be off-limits (and marked “Do Not Enter”) during the event. Participants are expected to carry their course map at all times and pay close attention to signage. Only registered participants, volunteers, and staff are allowed on the course.

RIDERS: Gravel, cyclocross, and mountain bikes are recommended (anything with 32mm tires and up). Road bikes are not suggested for this course. If you ask us, we will tell you not to bring your road bike.

Check-In/Out and Start/Finish Info: 

Participants are asked to arrive at least 30 min prior to their designated start time (waves times will be emailed), check-in with a staff member at registration (by the cabin), warm-up in designated areas (not on course), be prepared when called to the “staging area” at the start/finish, and sign-out with a staff member when finished.

We will have staggered start times (10-15 minutes) from 9:00am-12:00pm. Runners start at 9am. Long Purrito participants will start 9am-11am and Short Purrito participants will start 10am-12pm. The last start time will be at 12pm. Participants will be assigned specific time slots either individually or in small groups/teams with others based on requested time frame during registration (1-hour blocks). 

ALL team/group members must be present at check-in before proceeding to the start area. Participants may ride for as long as they wish but must be finished by the designated cut-off time (3pm).

Water, Aid Stations, Support: 

There is some access to water on-site, but it is limited so please plan on bringing your own water, food, and supplies for before, during, and after your ride. 

Temperatures can range in the area during the spring: it may be warm or cool (50-75 degrees), depending on the time of day . We will have water and some single-serving nutrition products available at the start/finish area and aid station checkpoints on course. 

Participants will be asked to carry whatever they need with them for the entire time they are on course (2-3 hours): water, nutrition, flat pack, map, cell phone, etc. There will be 5-10 checkpoints (depending on distance) on course along with at least one fully-staffed “aid station” if participants need assistance. Staff members and volunteers will have cell phones and radios, signs will clearly direct riders “Back to Start/Finish” if needed, and First Aid will be available at the start/finish area. In case of an emergency, dial 911 and alert a staff member or volunteer if possible. 

Food & Beverages: 

Water and single-serving nutrition items will be available at the start/finish area, as well as at one staffed aid station along the course at the top of the Kitten Crusher. Post-ride food (prepared box lunches) will be available for participants at an additional charge (approx $20/each) during registration and must be pre-ordered in advance. Beverages will be provided at NO additional charge. Outside food and drinks are welcome (BYOB). Please be conscientious of your surroundings and use the trash cans/recycling bins that are provided or take your trash with you. We want to be invited back again.

Property Info: LHFP is a private, working farm. NO participants will be permitted on-site prior to the event. The property will open at 8:00am on Saturday, April 24, 2027

Nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Locust Hill Farm & Preserve (LHFP) encompasses over 5,000 continuous acres of privately owned land. 

You will explore LHFP on private, gravel & dirt, farm roads that run along the Robinson River, pass serene creeks and ponds, weave through open fields, and cross wooded forest trails. The area is truly an adventure cyclist’s dream as well as a beautiful wildlife haven.

What makes this event unique is that it is 100% unpaved on private property. However, LHFP is a working farm that we have so graciously received permission to use from the landowners for our events. Entering ANY private sections of the property before race day will be considered trespassing and could seriously jeopardize the event, as well as our ability to host anything at this venue in the future (and will result in immediate disqualification). This is why we are careful when publicly posting any of our course routes, maps, GPS files, and Strava links. 

NOTE: We know that Dirty Kitten GPS tracks and Strava segments have been made public, but please remember that this is private property and LHFP roads may not be accessed any time outside of an official event. We ask that participants respect our landowner’s requests and know that the Dirty Kitten Crew does everything possible to ensure rider safety and provide accurate, up-to-date information before each event. 

Course Info: DKGC is a “choose-your-own-adventure” gravel event spanning approximately 20-40 miles and anywhere from 1,000 to 2,000 or more ft of elevation gain (depending on distance and route). 

The course is 100% unpaved with mostly gravel roads and dirt trails: the majority of terrain is on private farm roads with some dirt and grass double-track sections. It varies from smooth, groomed roads to rough, choppy areas with the possibility of mud if there is rain.

Participants choose their own route according to a course map provided at the start of the event. The majority of the course is on private farm roads with one section that follows a quiet, local, gravel road (Robinson River Road/Rt.721). Riders are expected to stay right of center and obey regular traffic laws while runners should stay on the left side of the road when on the public road section. There will be course signs and markings along the route.

Keep in mind that this is a working farm. Although we are in constant contact with the landowners and farmers to ensure everyone’s safety, there is always a possibility that you will encounter farm vehicles, livestock, and wildlife during the event. Eyes up and ears open at all times!!

Navigation Info: You won’t need GPS to navigate. The nature of Gralley Cat is an adventure-expedition style event. 

Participants are given a map to navigate to different locations on the property depending on their chosen course/distance (long or short). The course map will be simple and the boundaries will be very clearly marked. The checkpoints will not be hidden and signs on the course will point you in their direction. We will give names to the roads on the farm and intersections will be clearly marked so you always know where you are. There will be markings that you can follow to get back to the start at any time. Participants are expected to carry or download the course map and pay close attention to signage. 

NOTE: There is not a GPS route or map available for this event. Participants receive a paper or digital map of the course the morning of the event (no, you can't get a course map sooner so don't ask!) 

Awards & Prizes: TBA - Provided by our amazing event partners and sponsors

There will be no awards ceremony or podiums. Scores & rankings will be posted during the week following the event and any prizes will be mailed to participants a few weeks later. Giveaways will be available at the event with donations going to local, non-profit organizations in the area (TBD). Recipients must be present to win. 

Facilities: Port-o-pots and wash stations will be available along with Medical/First-Aid if needed. 

Photography: Renowned Event Photographer, Bruce Buckley, will be on-site taking photos throughout the day that will be available on his website for purchase after the event. 

Directions: Check-in and Start/Finish @ Locust Hill Farm & Preserve - 8070 N James Madison Highway, Rapidan, VA 22733 (turn off Rt. 15/James Madison Highway and continue down the gravel road). Cell phone service is spotty and unreliable in this area so please plan ahead!

Parking: Grass/field parking. When you enter the farm, continue on the gravel road until you see volunteers and parking signs. The landowners have asked that we park in specific areas so as not to damage crops or interfere with livestock so please be patient and respect our signs/volunteers when you arrive. 

Accommodations: If you wish to stay the weekend, there are several nearby hotels and local AirBnB/B&B options in the area. The Baymont by Wyndham in Culpeper (formerly Best Western Culpeper Inn) has given us a group rate for the weekend ($99/night). Call and mention the event: Dirty Kitten Spring Ride (540-825-1253) to receive our special group rate. The discount is available through March. You may cancel up to 24 hours before arrival.

Welcome back to the L.A. Tourist Race series for 2027!  You will be given  check points, TBD, that you will use to make your map.  At each checkpoint you will find a book, at that book tear out your corresponding race number and move on.  First one back with the correct numbered pages Wins! 

 

The basic tenants of the event to which all participants must adhere:

  1. Be fully self supported. Do not pre-stash or have others shuttle your food, water, tools or supplies while on the route. Plan accordingly.
  2. Know how to fix your stuff. No one will be sweeping the course. You need to be able to figure out your own extraction, if needed.
  3. Respect the course. Leave no trace ethos in place. Leave only tire tracks and footprints.
  4. Respect others. Other participants. Hikers. Equestrians. Forest Service.
  5. Like in years past, your participant number is the page you must grab at the check point from the book at that location. Wrong page or no page will equal "no check point".
  6. When on public and forst service roads, follow the rules of the road.
  7. Know how to navigate from point to point during the event. Never rely on others to be your naviagation.
  8. First aid and hydration are important. Prepare your own water and food or plan your food and water stops ahead of time.  

These races happen Rain or Shine, we do not cancel or postpone due to rain or snow.  These events can take you from sea level to over the 5k feet of elevation.  You may ride thru snow or cross streams and rivers so prepare yourself and keep an eye on the weather as event day approaches.  All registration sales are final

2026 Course Description:

Nestled in the Bavarian Alpine village of Helen, GA the ride starts in the heart of the North Georgia Mountains.  After rolling out of Helen the route hits the first timed segment at mile 2.5, where any riders with intentions of an overall podium finish will need to put their cards on the table from the start. The first time section immediately enters the mountainous area made famous by the 2003-2008 Tour de Georgia. In 2008, Unicoi Gap was the second to last climb on the approach to the race-deciding ascent up Brasstown Bald where Kanstantin Suitsou got the jump on Trent Lowe and Levi Leipheimer to win the event.  As riders tackle this timed section they cover over 7 miles and climb 1500ft to the top of Unicoi Gap. The climb is very gradual for several miles, before turning into a real alpine ascent. Enjoy the vistas of the Chattahoochee National Forest on the descent before turning left and climbing up and over Jack’s Gap.

A left turn on Richard Russell Scenic Hwy will put riders face to face with the 2nd timed section, Hogpen gap. Within 6.5 miles and another 1500ft, riders will reach the highest point on the course at 3469ft with ramps of 12%.  The views at the top of the surrounding peaks are breathtaking. Check your speed and be careful on the descent as there are many sharp turns. Enjoy the ride through the forest knowing that the hardest riding is behind you.

After tackling the two biggest climbs of the day riders will head east from Helen through Unicoi State Park. The route then hits the 3rd timed section at mile 46, comprised of rolling terrain for a 4 mile section. Riders then get to enjoy a non-timed section of the route for the next 30 miles as the route explore the area round Lake Burton and Seed Lake.  Be sure to save a bit of energy for the final time section, it only last just over 2 miles but at over 80 miles in to the day you'll need to find some go go power.

The route finishes back into the landmark town of Helen where, in 1969, local business owners collaborated to create what is now called “Bavaria in the Appalachians.” Just outside of Helen on the route is the Nacoochee Indian Mound, the center of the ancient Cherokee town of Gauxule, visited by Desoto in his search for gold.  Be sure to plan to stick around for beers, food and music served up at the finish line.

Welcome to Yachats, West Coast Gravel!

You’ve arrived at the “Gem of the Oregon Coast,” where towering Sitka spruces meet the crashing Pacific, and every sunset paints the sky in unforgettable hues.

This route is 20-30 minutes quicker than our Saturday event, with a remote start and finish 1 mile from Yachats! 

You're in for a special day!

Discover Your Coastal Playground

- Yachats State Recreation Area: Just steps from town, explore tide pools, picnic on seaside rocks, or simply listen to the surf roll in.

- Cape Perpetua: Drive a few miles south for panoramic ocean vistas, ancient forest trails like Amanda’s Trail, and Thor’s Well’s dramatic show of nature’s power.

- The Little Log Church & Museum: A charming historic venue perfect for a quiet moment of reflection—or even an impromptu photo op.

Savor Local Flavors

Fuel your adventures with fresh-caught seafood and local brews. Don’t miss Drift Inn or many other tempting places to dine  for a true taste of the coast.

Gather & Celebrate

Tonight, we’ll kick off at the Yachats Commons, the heart of community life—complete with ocean-inspired ambiance, local art, and excellent acoustics for our Graveo gathering.

We’re thrilled to host West Coast Gravel in our seaside hamlet. May your time here be filled with awe-inspiring landscapes, memorable connections, and the warm hospitality that makes Yachats so special. Welcome home to the Oregon Coast!

 

Mike and Andi Ripley and Crew

Full Hundo: This is the whole enchilada. Don't select this category without knowing that you are in for one hell of a challenge. This route is somewhere between 7,000 and 10,000 vertical feet of climbing (depending on the gps) and has broken many very experienced cyclists.

Metric Hundo:  If you want to come out and give this ride a try but you don't have the time, or the hundo is just a bit too much to bite off for you, this is a perfect ride.

Please read the notes below:

Welcome to the Event Page for the Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo 2027. This is the 14th running of this event and we are so happy to have you back. Thanks for giving this a try or for coming back for another year. I hope you have a great ride, but before then, take a look at all of the notes below. All of the info you need is laid out on this page.

1. Registration: Registration will open to the public at 12:01am on July 16 for a limited time.  If you want to make it in, make sure you are in line. If the category you want is sold out, try another one or jump into the waitlist. Last year almost everyone who stayed on the waitlist made it into the ride.

2. Waitlist: If you registered for the waitlist, please do not contact and ask where you are on the list. If someone drops out, you will be added and you will get a confirmation from Bike Reg. If you change your plans and do not want to be on the waitlist, remove yourself. If you are next in line and a spot opens up, you will be moved into the category and charged the full amount for the position.

3. Transfer/Cancel: Bike reg changed how they handle transfers, so you can now do it on your own for a limited amount of time. To prevent too many people from grabbing spots they won't use, there is a $15 transfer fee if you change your mind about the ride. 

There is only one category for people who might want to cancel. If you are not in that category, you can not cancel your entry but you can transfer it to a friend. The "I want in, but might want out" category offers a bailout for those that have complicated schedules and might not be able to make it. You will be able to get most of your money back and someone else will be able to ride. That is pretty cool and way more than most rides offer. PLEASE SEE DETAILED CANCELATION INFO AT THE BOTTOM OF THIS SECTION. 

4. General: Please make sure you have the proper physical training, the proper type of bike, the proper mindset for a long hard day in the saddle, and some technical acumen to take care of yourself incase you have an equipment malfunction. This ride covers a vast geographic area so if you are in trouble, you might have to wait a while for someone to come bail you out.

This is a rain or shine event. There are no refunds for your entry due to poor weather. 

The promoter retains the right to remove any rider that behaves in an unsafe or undesirable manner at any time. No refunds will be issued for improper behavior.

5. Friends, Family,Fans, and Supporters: We love when friends and family come out to support riders. This ride was founded on some solid friendships and support from my family. We will never forget that, so we want your people to come join us as well. They just need to follow a few rules. 1. Don't block the roads if you follow along in a vehicle. 2. Drive safely around all riders. 3. Come to the after party, but buy a meal ticket if you want to eat. 4. Clean up after yourself.  

6: Volunteers: We need you! This ride does not happen without tons of volunteers so please come and join us in all of the fun. We feed you, put you in the raffle, get you a cool shirt, and give you a fun job that shouldn't take all day. If you volunteer, you could ride next year for free (non transferable)! We do have some volunteer jobs that will also allow you to reid. Get in touch for more info.

7: Charity: The Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo believes in giving back. One dollar of each entry is donated to the The Pennsylvania Interscholastic Cycling League. In addition, the ride makes a donation to the Keystone Youth Mountain Bike Team. You will see many of the students and their parents out volunteering on the event weekend. 

8: Merchandise: We will have the chance to buy different types of merchandise over the next few months. We always strive to bring you some awesome goodies and this year is no different. 

9: Lodging  We are working on a lodging sponsor 
There are also plenty of other places to stay in the region. A large group camps Frances Slocum state park each year. 

10. Starrucca Crossing  is a gravel ride in NEPA that shares some of the same roads as LLWH, but it takes you out a bit further than LLWH ever could. It is a bit smaller ride, but tons of fun. 

11. GJE?  George J. Engleman is my dad. He is a big reason why this ride even exists. He gave me the love of exploration and of riding my bike. He was my number one volunteer. He passed away in November of 2016. I and the ride miss him dearly. If you see his initials on some merch, know that he is/was a very special person.

Tim, My Dad, Charles, and Dave on LLWH1

What is  Your CANCELLATION POLICY? 

 

We begin planning, permitting, and purchasing items for an event well in advance based on your pre-registration. Therefore we have a strict no refund policy. Be aware when you decide to register. We feel like our flexible transfer and change policies should accommodate most people and situations.

  1. CVP CANCELLATION POLICY No refunds, No exceptions.
    1. 45 Days Prior to the event:  Deadline to Defer to the following year.  Deferrals are good for 1 year only. You can not defer a second year. You may transfer your entry to another person if you have a deferred entry, but it must be done 30 days prior to the event.
    2.  10 Days Prior to the Event;
      1. You may transfer your entry to a different participant using the online transfer tool. Registration is transferable to the current event and year only. The deadline to transfer is 10 days prior to the event online.
      2. You may cancel your entry and receive a credit valued at 30% of your entry fee to use toward any CVP event within 1 year of cancellation. You MUST cancel no less than 10 days prior to the scheduled event.
    3. 9-0 Days before the Event:  Cancellations less than 10 days prior to an event and no-shows do not qualify for a credit.
  2. Transfers and Changes 

YOU Can now edit items on your registration if you have a Bikereg Account.  Racer name, phone, address, and email. You can also change the team category or team names. 

Transfers and Category Changes must be made through your BikeReg Account. Some actions are not allowed if you register as a guest. Change fees will apply.

If you change to a lessor distance you will not receive a refund on the price difference but we will not charge you a change fee.

If you change to a higher-priced category you will pay the change fee + the price difference.

3. Participant Insurance 

We highly suggest you purchase the insurance with your registration provided by BikeReg. This is separate from our company and will cover you in case of illness,  injury, or event cancelations due to weather and other unforeseen situations.

If you purchase the insurance and have a claim, call BikeReg directly. We can not process your claim. But, if you file one it will void any rights to a credit or transfer on our end. You can’t do both.

The Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race (PMBAR) is the absolute pinnacle of MTB Adventure Racing. A mix of brutal and beautiful, this test of spirit and camaraderie tasks teams of two racers to reach 4 of 5 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish as fast as possible. The team with the lowest overall time wins. Checkpoint locations remain secret until start-time and there is no suggested route. Routes vary between 50-80 miles, include 9,000-15,000 feet of climbing, and take 7-14 hours to complete.

PMBAR is held deep in the Pisgah National Forest, one of the most beautiful, rugged, and unforgiving areas in the nation. There will be little to no water or food support on course. Once you leave the start/finish you are on your own. There will be no drops, sag wagons, or other outside support available. Be prepared for any circumstances you may encounter including, but not limited to: medical emergencies, navigational errors, inoperable equipment, wild animals, and stinging/poisonous insects and plants.

6. Checkpoints may be reached in ANY ORDER.

8. Teams that reach FIVE (5) checkpoints will be awarded a TWO (2) HOUR time bonus.
9. There will be required gear checks on course. Teams will receive a TWO (2) HOUR time penalty for each piece of missing required gear.
10. The team with the LEAST OVERALL TIME (after bonuses and penalties) WINS!!!

Come and enjoy miles on miles of gravel roads around beautiful Wellsboro, Pennsylvania home of the PA Grand Canyon! We have another fresh course for 2027, a few roads overlap from previous years courses and we are changing the direction of travel on some favorite roads from years prior. This route, like every year, is a BEAST!

The Full MAMMOTH course is 136 miles and roughly 13,000 ft.+ of elevation gain to challenge even the most advanced riders. Those of you that choose to attempt the Full MAMMOTH will ride two separate non overlapping loops. Both loops begin and end at the same place in downtown Wellsboro. The morning loop is 71 miles in length and afternoon is 65 miles. Breakfast, lunch, dinner  and two aid stops are included with this option.

Half MAMMOTH riders will just ride the 71 mile morning loop along with the Full MAMMOTH riders but will be done riding after the morning loop. Breakfast, lunch and the morning aid stop are included with this option.

The Quarter MAMMOTH Route is an abbreviated version of what the Half MAMMOTH Route riders are doing. You still get breakfast and lunch as well as stopping at Aid 1 for espresso and baked goods but you only ride 29 miles and climb about 3000 ft. Not necessarily "beginner friendly" but still a challenge without absolutely destroying yourself.  Breakfast, lunch and the morning aid stop are included with this option.

All food choices are selected in the registration process. There will be Vegan options available at all meals and aid stations.

Roughly halfway through each loop there will be an absolute banger of an aid station. We work with local businesses to provide hearty food at aid stations, as well as the essentials. The morning aid stop is included with all registrations. The afternoon stop is included with only Full MAMMOTH Registrations.

Please keep in mind that there will be a support vehicle patrolling the course as well as sweep riders bringing up the rear but we highly recommend that you carry what you need for  roughly  35 mile stretches.

*THIS EVENT WILL HAPPEN RAIN OR SHINE.  We DO NOT offer refunds or deferrals as all the event food and promotional items are paid for and ordered ahead of time. PLEASE CONSIDER ADDING REG INSURANCE OFFERED THROUGH BIKEREG IF YOU ARE WORRIED ABOUT WEATHER ETC. AND GETTING REFUNDED.

*We try our best to mark this monster route but the weather the previous days to the event really can dictate how well it is marked. The safest option is to use a bicycle computer with navigation or a phone app like Komoot or RWGPS for navigation. A GPX file will be sent to the email you use to register a few weeks prior to the event.

All event day check in, meals, and after ride hang out will all be centralized around the Patterson Trailhead building.

Free parking is available at this venue. If you stay at the Hotels located in downtown Wellsboro you will only be about a 2 minute bicycle ride from the Start/Mid/Finish and riding down would leave more spots available for those that drove in, this is not a requirement just a suggestion.

If you have any additional questions please feel free to email us or PM us on Facebook or Instagram also keep an eye out on mammothendurancegravel.com for resources and information.

Sixteenth Annual Belgian Waffle Ride California

 

May 1–2, 2027 | San Diego County, California

Hell of the North County

Welkom to the sixteenth annual Belgian Waffle Ride California. The one that started it all returns May 1–2, 2027, for another weekend of bikes, beautiful bad judgment and the kind of post-ride storytelling that gets better with every Belgian ale.

The Hell of the North (County) has always been built around Unroad: a course that refuses to settle on one surface or let riders settle into one rhythm. Pavement gives way to dirt, sand and rocky sectors. Climbs interrupt conversations. Technical terrain asks questions your training plan may have neglected.

Waffle, Wafer and Wanna offer three ways into the experience, bringing accomplished racers and everyday riders together over the same North County terrain. The festival gives friends, families and cycling partners a place to gather before the ride and stay long after it. Venue and weekend programming will be announced as they are finalized.

Weekend experience

The weekend brings together rider check-in, the Unroad Expo, riding and the post-ride gathering. Meet the brands, catch up with your people, eat waffles and leave enough time for the stories afterward. The detailed 2027 program, venue and start times will be announced on the event page.

EventName: Gravel Roll - Veloboros at Phinizy Swamp
EventNotes:
The Ouroboros is an ancient Greek symbol of a serpent eating its own tail. It is a symbol of the endless cycle of renewal. As you know, the Gravel Roll is always looking for new things, new places, new adventures and, most of all, new fun.
 

Welcome to Veloboros at Phinizy Swamp, a brand-new gravel cycling experience coming to Augusta, Georgia on May 1, 2027.
What better place to experience the endless cycle than in an honest-to-goodness swamp? There are alligators, wildlife, and plenty of questionable decisions to be made.


We’re not going to hold you to traditional race distances. Instead, you can see how many laps of the swamp you can complete.
Choose your adventure: each one with a little more…souciant of the Snake Eating Its Tail.
 

3-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Short Course
5-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Intermediate Course
7-Hour Veloboros - Usual Gravel Roll Long Course

Each lap is about 6.5 miles of 100% unpaved, traffic-free riding through Phinizy Swamp.

Ride as many laps as you can as a solo rider or put together a team of up to six riders to complete as many laps as possible in a relay fashion.
Whether you are trying to win the race or just trying to finish the event, there is a place for you in the swamp.
Every Lap Leads Back to the Party.


At the heart of Veloboros is our central Party Village, where every lap begins and ends. The FOUR Fs of your friends, family, food, and festivities are never more than one lap away. So complete another loop, grab some food, socialize with your crew, or take a break before heading back out on the course. Or, just put your head down and grind away on your stem. We don’t care how you complete the event, as long as you are having fun. And, if you make a wrong turn, don’t worry about getting lost, because you can get a ride behind Uncle Orville’s airboat back on course!
 

You decide how seriously to take the challenge. We're just here to make sure you have a good time.

We have some swampy shenanigans in store as well.


Phinizy Swamp is home to an incredible collection of birds, alligators, and other wildlife, and we're incorporating that natural wonder into the experience with a swamp-themed scavenger hunt and other surprises throughout the day.

Keep your eyes open. You never know what you'll spot between laps.


Our goal for the day is a great day of bikes, friends, nature and fun. You can come to race, you can come to ride, or you can come to hang out with friends.
This being the very first year we are going to limit registration to 150 riders for year one. We want to make sure how many folks we can really have a good time with in the swamp.


The Details
Saturday, May 1, 2027
Phinizy Swamp | Augusta, Georgia
3-, 5-, and 7-hour challenges | Solo or teams of up to six
Approximately 6.5-mile loop | 100% unpaved | Closed to motor vehicle traffic

So gather your crew, circle the date, and prepare to go around in circles for a very good reason.

Course and Format Overview:

  • Total Distance: 240 miles across 12 laps of 20 miles

  • Lap Cutoff: Every lap starts precisely every 120 minutes

  • First Bell: Saturday, May 1, 2027 at 10:00 AM sharp

  • Profile: Rolling ridges, fast gravel, and stretches of valley pavement with roughly 950 feet of climbing per lap

  • Venue: Pea Ridge Bike Camp, 10542 Blue Jay Road, Pea Ridge, Arkansas 72751

Staging and Pit Setup: Every registered Reckonneur receives space for one 10x10 pop up tent inside the rider pit area to manage gear, hydration, and nutrition during the event. Dedicated pit space is included with your entry.

Camping and Rig Parking: If you plan to arrive on Friday, stay through Sunday, or require space for an RV, vehicle rig, or pit crew encampment, you must book an official campsite in advance through Hipcamp. Space at Pea Ridge Bike Camp is limited, so reserve early if you need overnight accommodations.

Category Details (For the Single Reckonneur Entry):

  • Category Name: The Reckonneur

  • Distance: 240 Miles (12 Laps)

  • Description: The solitary entry category for all starters. Toe the line, manage the clock, and survive the toll.

Event Rules and Rider Requirements:

This is a true grassroots, do it yourself adventure challenge. No roads are closed for this event, and all participants must obey standard rules of the road at all times. Expect open rural traffic, county intersections, and working farmland along the route. Every rider must be fully self reliant on course.

There are no relay teams, no tag teaming, and no split entries. Every Reckonneur registers, rides, and faces the clock as an individual. You must complete every lap under your own power to remain in contention. Even the race organizer is toeing the line and riding the full event right alongside you.

Lighting and Night Riding: As the sun drops over the ridges, darkness sets in quickly on the rural backroads. Solid forward white lights and rear red blinkers are mandatory equipment for any lap undertaken between dusk and dawn. No light, no ride. 

Your front light must have sufficient output to navigate unlit gravel roads, potholes, and steep descents safely at speed. Rear lights must be visible from a significant distance to warn approaching motorists. Bring extra batteries, backup lights, or charging banks to keep your lighting operational throughout the entire night. Course marshals will pull any rider attempting to start a night lap without adequate illumination.
