EventName: The 2027 Massochistah! (A Fundraiser For Youth and Adaptive Cycling)
EventNotes:
It's 2027, all over again!!!

 

 

Join Northampton Cycling Club for an exploration of the most scenic and challenging roads in western Massachusetts while supporting the expansion of cycling for all people in Hampshire and Franklin County.

 

 

ALL proceeds fund youth and adaptive cycling programs in Hampshire and Franklin County. We are completely volunteer-run to maximize support for these programs.

 

*253 years of tradition (give or take 249 years)

 

 

THE ETHOS

 

The Massochistah offers four distinct courses – each with its own character, all designed to challenge you. The longer courses were originally envisioned as spring warm-ups for Rasputitsa (RIP) and major gravel events. The shorter courses serve as an introduction to the great riding to be found in Western Massachusetts. 

 

While not a race, you will find PLENTY of motivation and maybe a few friendly rivalries along the way. In the past some very serious riders have used this as race prep for Rasputitsa, Unbound, Traka, etc.  The competitive spirit is alive and well here, particularly on the longer rides.  That said, this is not a race!  You will be riding on public roads and rights of way open to other users including walkers, cyclists, equestrians and motorized users.  Be aware of your surroundings at all times.  It is up to you to ensure crossing an intersection or a challenging section of trail is safe and within your abilities. 

 

Similarly, navigation is part of the challenge of these rides. If you are riding the MPC or Hurty, expect to receive a Ride with GPS route in the days before the event.  It is up to you to download the route (and the free app, if needed) to your smartphone, cycling computer or other device. We strongly recommend completing the download before traveling to the event.  The closer you get to the venue, the less reliable cell reception becomes. We will not have the resources to help you download the file and set up the app or your cycling computer when you arrive. You should have a strong working knowledge of the device you intend to use for navigation.  MPC and Hurty routes are not marked, so it is up to you to navigate the loop successfully!

If you are riding the Dirty or Flirty, the route will be marked. You will also be provided with a Ride with GPS file prior to the event and a cue sheet when you check-in.  Because route markings may move, disappear, or prove otherwise inaccurate, we strongly encourage Dirty and Flirty riders to track their own progress using a digital device or their cue sheet in addition to following route markers.  Navigating the short courses will be much less complicated than the long routes, but it is still possible to get lost!

 

You will experience a good bit of climbing, regardless of the route. The paved sections will be mostly low-traffic, although occasionally crossing or briefly following busier roadways is unavoidable.  The unpaved sections will range from smooth, recently-packed gravel to overgrown two-track jeep trails.  Some are maintained annually, but many are not.  You can expect to encounter surfaces such as loose rocks, tree roots, rock slabs, mud, slippery rocks and standing water, not to mention potholes and washboard.  We do our best to ensure routes are free of large logs or blow-downs, but cannot guarantee this.  Hills can be gentle or absurdly steep, but most are somewhere in-between.  Be ready to dismount your bike to get over an obstacle, up a hill, or through a slick situation.  Come prepared and willing to embrace the suck, even on the shorter rides.  Expect to get hungry, tired and dirty.

 

Of course, no suffering goes unrewarded!  Hot food, local beer, non-alcoholic beverages, and a full post-ride party are waiting for you back in Goshen!!

 

 

2027 ROUTES*

 

THE MARGARET PIWONKA CHALLENGE (aka MPC) — 8:00am Start

Course- TBD

The crown jewel. The beast. This is where reputations are made (mainly for crying).

Approximately 75 miles of jeep track, dirt roads, and pavement connectors. Some singletrack and hike-a-bike sections are possible. Plan on at least 120 ft/mi of elevation gain. If you don't know what that means, choose a different course.

 

What you need: A well-tuned bike with big tires (40mm+), big gears, and the skills and fitness to finish within 9 hours (approximate moving speed: 10mph). Most riders clock 5-7 hours on course.

The reality check: Due to the remote nature of portions of this route, be comfortable going 2.5-3 hours between fully stocked aid stations. If your bike breaks or you crash, it's a long walk—or longer wait—until help arrives. There will be time cutoffs at each of the two aid stations to ensure everyone gets a warm meal at the end.

The promise: An emailed, RWGPS route at least two days ahead of the event, two stocked aid stations and… an adventure. You'll love it. You’ll hate us. Then you’ll love us again when you get to the party at the finish line

 

THE HURTY — 9:00am Start

Course- TBD

The classic. Approximately 50 miles of quality dirt and pavement with brutal-but-doable climbs. Expect at least 100'/mi of elevation gain. This may not be the longest event, but it'll hurt just the same.

 

What you need: We recommend a gravel bike with well-functioning disc brakes and 35-45mm tires, though this route goes just fine on both road and gravel setups. The one you should choose depends on conditions and your comfort level on loose or washed-out descents. Most riders finish in 3.5-5 hours.

The promise: Stocked aid stations strategically placed 1.5-2 hours apart. At least one sag wagon on course for emergencies. A great ride and maybe some leg cramps to laugh about at the party. 

 

THE DIRTY — 10:00am Start

Course- TBD

The Dirty is a 25ish mile introduction, for those who want to flirt with hill town gravel without fear of major commitment; as our shortest option, it is also designed to be accessible for younger riders (accompanied by their adults).

 

What you need:  Just about any well-maintained bike with good gears and brakes.  Hybrid bikes, kids’ bikes, mountain bikes, road, gravel, CX should all work just great.  Just make sure you aren’t running some ultra-light tires that will deflate out of fear if they come within 5 feet of a rock – you gram-counters know who you are. It’s best to bring some snacks and a water bottle or two along with you to maintain energy and hydration.  During the ride the aid station always seem so very far away!

The promise: Both routes offer varied terrain with a little bit of everything. Expect to climb, but also to soak in beautiful spring scenery in western Massachusetts.  At least one stocked aid station and sag wagon support will be available.  Most riders finish in 2-3.5 hours.  IMPORTANT: Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult, regardless of route.

 *We have moved the event from Ashfield to Goshen – new location, but same great routes!

 

WEATHER & CONDITIONS

 

The Massochistah is an early-season event. In the hill towns, early season can mean many different weather conditions – sometimes all of them on the same day!

 

Come prepared for winter conditions, but pack sunscreen and electrolytes for heat. Expect roads in all types of shape: perfect, muddy, snow covered, flooded, bone dry…. welcome to spring in Western New England.  This ain’t Boston.   Plan accordingly. 

 

Organizers will communicate course updates and conditions the week of the event and reserve the right to shorten routes due to extremely foul weather or impassable sections. 

 

The event will only be cancelled if local or state authorities recommend it, or if Massachusetts declares a state of emergency in the area. This is just about the only condition when we will consider issuing refunds, or offer entry carry-over to next year.  Since this event is a fundraiser, no refunds will be made if you decide not to ride due to bad weather or weather-related course modifications.  Thanks for understanding!

Welcome to the Red Fondo. We'd love for you to join us in this beautiful region of the Bluegrass State for our event. See Q&A below for more info.

What kind of event is this?

This is a Gran Fondo with all paved roads. See the Red Fondo Instagram for more details of what the course looks like. It will be mass start group event. Results based on finish line placing. First person across the line wins and so on. 

What kind of bike should I use?

A road or gravel bike with climbing gears. All routes will be completely paved, though the pavement may be rough in sections. I'd opt for a 30-40mm road tire or slick gravel tire. You definitely want to have enough gears for some of the steep climbs out on course. I ride my Lauf Uthald with a 2x setup to give me sufficient gears for climbing and descending. No aero bars. 

What's the course like?

Amazing. Beautiful. Challenging. The roads are narrow and winding and have very little traffic. The course will be open to traffic and we may have a lead car to improve safety for the front group (TBD). The course will be challenging with several very steep climbs. Bring your climbing gears! Official courses will be released as we get closer to the day of the race.

Course will not be marked. Each rider is responsible for downloading and following the route on their bike computer.

Where is it?

The Red River Gorge is known for it's amazing hiking and climbing. I'd highly recommend everyone making a weekend out of this and enjoying the great outdoors the Gorge has to offer. The Natural Bridge trail is a must see and is an easy 1 mile hike. The start and finish of the race will take place at Bowen Elementary in Bowen, KY. 

What are the categories?

3 Course options to choose from including a 35 mile, 65 mile and 120 mile option. Each distance will include a Men's, Masters Men 40+ and Women's category. All categories and distances will start together. The split offs for each distance are far enough into the route that it shouldn't cause any issues. We will do 9 podiums. Male, Female & Masters podiums for each distance.

What are the rules?

Your safety is our #1 priority. We are racing on open roads. The roads are narrow and there are a lot of blind turns so please stay aware and stay safe. Most of the roads do not have a yellow line, but stay on the right side of the road when possible to avoid any potential accidents with vehicles on course. If the group is big enough I'd like to have a lead moto or lead car to improve safety for the front group. TBD. 

You can only take feeds at the designated feed zones. Or at stores or gas stations along the route.

No littering.

Be kind to your fellow racers. 

The race director has the discretion to relegate or disqualify riders.

Will there be food?

Each registered rider will receive a post-race meal. It will be a sub sandwiches with sides, desserts & drinks. All riders will receive a Red Fondo pint glass.

What about Aid Stations?

More information about feed zones and feed zone rules will come out once the routes are finalized.

 

If you have any more questions don't hesitate to reach out. Thanks!

Eighth Annual Belgian Waffle Ride Utah presented by BZI

May 14–15, 2027 | Cedar City, Utah

Hell of the South West

The eighth annual BWR Utah returns to Cedar City May 14–15, 2027, giving the Hell of the South (West) a new chapter and a new date in May.

Cedar City remains our high-desert home for long gravel sectors, open views and riding at altitude. The 2026 course introduced extensive new Unroad terrain, trading the earlier technical singletrack emphasis for a route that rewarded pacing, power and the ability to keep making good decisions as the day wore on.

Weekend experience

The weekend brings together rider check-in, the Unroad Expo, riding and the post-ride gathering. Meet the brands, catch up with your people, eat waffles and leave enough time for the stories afterward. The detailed 2027 program, venue and start times will be announced on the event page.

Description (UCI Qualifying)

The Belgian Waffle Ride Utah – Cedar City is proud to serve as an official qualifier for the UCI Gravel World Series (GWS), bringing world-class gravel racing to the spectacular terrain of Southern Utah on May 14–15, 2027.

As part of the UCI Gravel World Series, BWR Utah offers riders the opportunity to qualify for the UCI Gravel World Championships, competing against some of the best gravel athletes from around the world.

Qualification for the World Championships is determined by age group and gender, including Elite men's and women's categories for eligible UCI-licensed riders. The top 25% of finishers in each qualifying category earn the opportunity to compete at the World Championships. Age-group qualification begins with the 19–34 category, followed by five-year age brackets (35–39, 40–44, etc.) through the oldest participating age group.

Set against the breathtaking red rock landscapes and rugged high-desert terrain of Cedar City, Belgian Waffle Ride Utah delivers the challenging and unforgettable experience that has made BWR one of the most recognized gravel cycling events in North America.

The event will feature designated qualifying courses tailored to UCI age and gender categories, combining demanding gravel roads, challenging climbs, high-altitude terrain, and the signature Belgian Waffle Ride experience.

Whether chasing a coveted spot at the UCI Gravel World Championships or simply taking on an extraordinary gravel challenge, BWR Utah offers an opportunity to race, qualify, and experience the very best of Southern Utah gravel.

Eighth Annual BWR Utah Rider Information

 

Rider perks

The BWR rider offering includes the following. Utah’s awards and eligibility will follow the final event regulations.

  • BWR musette bag from Neversecond with race-day essentials and sponsor swag
  • BWR branded memento or BWR Bucks for use with participating partners
  • Race number and RFID timing tag for the official finishing time
  • Pre- and post-ride waffles, coffee and beverages
  • Stocked feed zones with hydration and nutrition, including Neversecond
  • Marked courses, traffic control at designated locations and on-course support
  • Post-ride beer and the BWR community celebration
  • Finisher’s trophy beer, with the offering determined by distance and event
  • Unroad Expo access and opportunities to meet cycling brands and partners
  • Bragging rights and more than enough material for the next group ride
  • Podium recognition and awards according to the published 2027 BWR category rules

Official BWR t-shirts, apparel and branded gear will be available through registration and the BWR merchandise area at the expo.

The Short Line Shuffle-18 Mile:

Saddle up for a laid-back ride on The Short Line Shuffle – 18 Mile. Designed for riders who want to soak in the scenery without the strain, this out-and-back course offers a smooth and approachable introduction to gravel riding.

With just around 90 feet of elevation gain, this route keeps things gentle and enjoyable, making it perfect for beginners, families, or anyone looking for a relaxed spin. You’ll cruise primarily along the scenic Cowboy Trail, where wide-open skies and peaceful stretches of Nebraska countryside set the tone for a true prairie experience.

Midway through your journey, you’ll roll into Battle Creek for a convenient stop—an ideal chance to rest, refuel, and take in a bit of small-town charm before heading back the way you came.

Whether you're new to gravel or just in it for a calm, easy ride, The Short Line Shuffle delivers a welcoming adventure with just the right touch of cowboy spirit.

 

Tracks and Tread 50K:

 

Saddle up for the heart of the Cowboy Gravel Grinder with the Tracks and Tread 50K—a perfect blend of scenic cruising and rewarding effort. This 50-kilometer route delivers approximately 500 feet of elevation gain, offering a smooth yet engaging ride for gravel cyclists of all levels.

Rolling out from the brewery, riders will head south into Nebraska’s wide-open countryside, where quiet gravel roads stretch across gently rolling terrain. Expect sweeping views, fresh country air, and the rhythmic crunch of gravel beneath your tires as you find your pace.

The route leads you toward Battle Creek, guiding you through a landscape that feels both rugged and peaceful. With manageable climbs and long, flowing stretches, this course is designed to keep you moving while still giving you time to take in the surroundings.

After reaching the turnaround, you’ll retrace your path back north, finishing where it all began—at the brewery—where a well-earned drink and camaraderie await.

Whether you're pushing your limits or enjoying the ride, the Tracks and Tread 50K captures the spirit of gravel riding: freedom, grit, and just the right amount of adventure.

 

The Frontier Fondo - 100K Route

Saddle up for the ultimate prairie adventure on The Frontier Fondo, the signature 100K route of the Cowboy Gravel Grinder. Rolling out from the brewery, riders head south into the heart of wide-open country, where the gravel stretches endlessly beneath big Nebraska skies.

With roughly 1,300 feet of elevation gain, this route offers a perfect balance of challenge and flow—long, steady rollers, punchy climbs, and rewarding descents that keep your legs working and your spirit soaring. Along the way, you’ll wind through quiet country roads, pass through charming small towns, and take in sweeping scenic views that define the frontier landscape.

Expect a ride that feels both rugged and welcoming—where every mile tells a story, every hill reveals a new horizon, and every turn reminds you why gravel riding is as much about the journey as the finish line.

The Frontier Fondo isn’t just a ride—it’s a full immersion into the soul of gravel country.

EventNotes:
Starrucca Crossing is back again for 2027 from the creators of Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo. This is the most remote course we have come up with that takes riders into some of the beauty of the Endless Mountains/Northern Tier of Pennsylvania. We start in the two stoplight town of Montrose, Pa and head right out onto gravel roads through farms, along creeks, and up and down valleys. We visit the towns of Montrose, Hop Bottom, Brooklyn, and Nicholson each with their own unique history. Come check out our 30, 50, 75, and 100 mile routes on Ride with GPS. 

The ride has full support in terms of rest stops, roving mechanics/SAG and some great pizza and drinks at the Montrose VFW when you are done. 

Due to the lack of road signs (particularly on the secondary roads) and poor cell phone signal reliability, use of GPS (downloaded and saved to your device in advance) is essential. 

What is  Your CANCELLATION POLICY? 

No refunds, No exceptions.

We begin planning, permitting,  and purchasing items for an event well in advance based on your pre-registration. Therefore we have a strict no refund policy. Be aware when you decide to register. We feel like our flexible transfer and change policies should accommodate most people and situations.

  1. CVP CANCELLATION POLICY No refunds, No exceptions.
    1. 45 Days Prior to the event:  Deadline to Defer to the following year. A fee may apply. You must transfer to the same race and Category. Deferrals are good for 1 year only. You can not defer a second year. You may transfer your entry to another person if you have a deferred entry, but it must be done 30 days prior to the event.
    2.  10 Days Prior to the Event;
      1. You may transfer your entry to a different participant using the online transfer tool. Registration is transferable to the current event and year only. The deadline to Transfer is 10 days prior to the event online.
      2. You may change to a different category for a fee. The last day to make changes is 10 days prior to the ride.
      3. If there is a waitlist in your category, you may request a credit or refund if there is a person who can take your spot off the waitlist.
      4. You may cancel your entry and receive a credit valued at 30% of your entry fee to use toward any CVP event within 1 year of cancellation. You MUST cancel no less than 10 days prior to the scheduled event.
    3. 9-0 Days before the Event:  Cancellations less than 10 days prior to an event and no-shows do not qualify for a credit.
  2. Transfers and Changes 

YOU Can now edit items on your registration if you have a Bikereg Account.  Racer name, phone, address, and email. You can also change the team category or team names. 

Transfers and Category Changes must be made through your BikeReg Account. Some actions are not allowed if you register as a guest. Change fees will apply.

If you change to a lessor distance you will not receive a refund on the price difference but we will not charge you a change fee.

If you change to a higher-priced category you will pay the change fee + the price difference.

3. Participant Insurance 

We highly suggest you purchase the insurance with your registration provided by BikeReg. This is separate from our company and will cover you in case of illness,  injury, or event cancelations due to weather and other unforeseen situations.

If you purchase the insurance and have a claim, call BikeReg directly. We can not process your claim. But, if you file one it will void any rights to a credit or transfer on our end. You can’t do both.

EventAddress: Upper Greenhorn Park, Greenhorn Rd, Yreka, CA 96097
EventName: Siskiyou Scenic Bicycle Tour 2027/ Greenhorn Gravel Grinder
EventNotes:
Yreka, CA is located 22 miles south of the Oregon border on I-5 and is the county seat of Siskiyou County. Yreka's elevation is 2,595 ft. May is very pleasant with many wildflowers, but because of the elevation and the elevations you may climb, it is always best to be prepared for inclement weather. Siskiyou County is known for the Mt. Shasta Ski and Recreation Area, the Marble Mountain & Trinity Alps Wilderness Areas, trails, camping, bicycle touring and events, fishing, river rafting, historical districts, and also has a casino. Our website is www.siskiyouscenic.com. This is an open course road ride event. There are potholes, obstacles, railroad tracks, vehicles, traffic lights, signs, etc. Cyclists are responsible to be alert and obey all traffic laws. This event takes place no matter what the weather is like. Cyclists not comfortable riding under these conditions should not participate in the event.

The event is May 15th and 16th, 2027. There are 8 different rides. The longest is 102 miles, all pavement with 5,902 ft. of elev. gain, and goes over Forest Mountain into and through Scott Valley then over Gazelle Mountain and back to Yreka.This is our old traditional Siskiyou Century route. Challenging but gorgeous scenery.  There is a metric century, 67 mile route, all pavement, which goes to Edgewood and then back north, with 2,303 ft. of elevation gain- the same as last year's ride.  The 40 mile, all pavement route is 1,534 ft of elevation gain through Shasta Valley. The 21 mile  all pavement ride is 1,055 ft. of elevation gain through parts of Shasta Valley and Montague. We have 2 gravel rides on Sunday May 16th sponsored by the Jefferson Mountain Bike Association. A 39 mile mostly gravel route over Greenhorn Summit with 3 good hill climbs- with 4,114 ft. of elevation gain.  And a 62 mile mostly gravel route with 6,474 ft. of elevation gain over Greenhorn Summit into Ft. Jones then over Scarface and back to the west side of Shasta Valley. There is incredible scenery on all routes.  There is a $20 discount for registering for events both days.

We have an all pavement ride of 29 to 39 miles on Sunday May 16th through Scott Valley and Quartz Valley with 1,033- 1,159 ft. of elevation gain that will start in Fort Jones at the Forest Service parking lot, and also a part gravel route on Saturday May 15th of 58 miles through Shasta Valley with 2,279 ft. of elevation gain,  so that those who only ride 1 type of bike can enjoy 2 days of riding in Siskiyou County, or maybe you want to do 1 day of pavement and 1 day of gravel. 

All rides, except the Sunday pavement ride, start and finish at Upper Greenhorn Park, on Greenhorn Rd. In Yreka. There will be a mass start with police escort through Yreka, for the Saturday rides.   Entry fees, 102 mile- $95, 67 mile-$85, 40 mile- $65, 21 mile- $40. Sunday gravel rides, 62 mile $85, 39 mile $65. The Saturday gravel ride- $75 and Sunday pavement ride- $60. There will be a $10 late registration fee after May 1st. There will be multiple rest stops with food and drinks, and sag wagon support for all the routes. There will be an end of ride meal catered and served between 11am and 4pm on Saturday and 12-4 on Sunday. It will be much different than last year's meal- better! Beer will be available for purchase at the park both days.  Event T-shirts are available for $25 each. You must complete your ride by 4pm each day or you will be picked up by the sag wagon and returned to the park. All services end after 4:30pm. 

Tent or camper van camping will be available at Greenhorn Park Friday May 14th and Saturday May 15th for $20/night per unit. There are bathrooms, but no showers on site, however showers will be available at our local YMCA for no charge. There are several RV parks in Yreka with full hook-ups for RV's.

You may pick up your packets Friday May 14th at Upper Greenhorn Park between 5-7pm, and starting at 6am on May 15th, and 7am on Sunday May 16th. If you are riding the Sunday all pavement ride, you may pick up your packet at the Forest Service parking lot starting at 8:30am, if not picked up prior to then at Greenhorn Park. 

The route descriptions and maps may be found on our website www.siskiyouscenic.com or on RidewithGPS.com under the Siskiyou Scenic Bicycle Tour 2027. This ride is put on by the Rotary Club of Yreka, and provides funds for community projects and scholarships for our graduating high school students. There will be prizes for oldest, youngest, farthest away, 1st registration and largest group in each category.

EventNotes:
The Calvins Challenge Event for 2027 - May 15-16

I am very excited to announce that the Calvins Challenge event is back again in 2027 after being an ever greater success in 2026.

We are also incredibly fortunate enough to have it at the same Shawnee High School location! The format for the 100 mile, 6-hr, 12-hr and 24-hr events will be the same as 2026 - utilizing a long and short loop! There will be drafting, non-drafting, and self-supported categories. For insurance issues: I must clearly state that this is not a race. Each rider is riding for personal best in their own category.

What’s New: Nicer and shorter daytime loop.

Sadly due to the continued deterioration of many sections of the original 50-mile loop I do not feel it is safe any longer. So right after the event in May I scouted, rode, and video’d some possible replacement routes. And the winner is:

The 15.0 mile daytime loop (all events): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54088467

RAAM Qualifier (RQ): Again for 2026 - Calvins Challenge 24-hour non-drafting event will be a RAAM qualifier. The RQ Standard is 380 miles for men and 350 miles for women and 60+ men.

Where is it:

The hub of the event will be the Shawnee High School (1675 E Possum Rd, Springfield, OH 45502) If you rode in Calvin’s 2016 or earlier or 2024-25 you will recognize it. The start/finish/lap timing and crew setup will be at the back of the building in the parking lots. There is traffic circle at the intersection of Selma Pike and E Possum Rd (at the NE corner of the school) - which is a welcome addition. Here is a view of that area: Yellow path indicates bike route on road and purple is timing and crew setup. Riders will come into school back parking lot off of E Possum Rd - and then turn right on to Selma Pike

Important Dates:

  • Dec 31, 2026 - Last Day for early bird registration
  • April 1, 2027 - Last Day to order a custom Calvin’s t-shirt or Jersey
  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) 5pm - Final day for online registration
  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) - 4pm - 7pm - Packet pickup and late registration
  • May 15, 2027 (Sat) - 5am-6am - event day packet pickup and late registration

Packet Pickup and on-site Registration:

New for 2027 - No more paper waivers - I will email you a link you can us electronically sign your waiver. Then about 2 weeks before the event I will email you your digital packet including your bib # and all other info about the event. All you will have to do is show up Fri from 4-7 or Sat from 6-7 to get your bike tag and your RFID tag - then ride!

Your packet up is at the Shawnee High School Football concession stand (behind the school)

  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) - 4pm - 7pm - Packet pickup and late registration
  • May 15, 2027 (Sat) - 5am-6am - Event day packet pickup and late registration                      

Awards and snacks:

Awards will be given at the finish line area after each event as soon as results can be tabulated - Estimating 15-30 minutes after last rider in

I will provide some after ride snacks and water for the riders and crew. If you would like to bring anything to share there will be some tables to put in on. I will also work on getting some food trucks there this year too!

The courses:

  • The original 50.5 daytime loop (rider’s choice) : https://ridewithgps.com/routes/7576957
    • video: https://youtu.be/5vimwlyMqGs
  • The new 15.0 mile daytime loop (all events): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54088467
    • video: https://youtu.be/BK-nGAjvYj0
  • The original 6.8 mile finishing loop:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/7576965
    • video: https://youtu.be/7wceJTSHq3I

The events: 4 UltraCycling & 3 Time Trial Events

There will be 4 UltraCycling events: 100 Mile, 6-hour, 12-hour, & 24-hour.

There will be 3 Time Trial events: 7-Mile, 15-Mile, and 50-Mile Time Trial

All events will have the following categories: gender, 5-yr age-groups, all bike types, supported or unsupported, and solo as well as 2 thru 8 rider teams. There is something for everyone! The UltraCycling events will also have non-drafting or drafting categories.

The Century will ride 6 loops of the 15.0 mile loop and 1 loop of the 6.8 mile loop, or 2 loops of the original 50.5 mile loop (at your own peril).

The 6, & 12-hour events will all ride the 15 mile loop as many times as they can. When they feel they would not be able to complete another 15 mile loop, they will transition to the 6.8 mile loop until their event time is completed.

The 24 Hour riders will also ride the 15 mile loop as many times as they can until dark. At this time they can decide to continue to ride the 15 mile loop or switch to the 6.8 mile loop. We will make the assumption that you will ride the 6.8 loop unless you tell the timer you are going to do the 15 mile. This is so we will give you the proper credit for the loop you are riding. If you decide to ride the 15 through the night, then once you cannot complete the loop before your time expires please transition to the 6.8 mile loop until your 24 hours is completed.

Each of the Time Trials events (7, 15, & 50 miles) - Each ride one lap of each of the 3 courses (described below). All riders will leave every 15 secs immediately after all the UltraCycling riders leave. Approx 7:05am

Note: For all timed events - you must complete the loop you are on when your time expires. Your average speed on this final loop will be used to determine your prorated distance for the amount of the time you rode that loop before your timed event expires. Even if you miss-judged how long it would take you to complete one of the longer loops and your time expired while you were riding one of them, complete the loop and your distance will be prorated.

Mechanicals and/or race abandonment before completing a full lap

If you have a mechanical and had to call your crew to help and had to return to the school, you must return to the spot you stopped (via vehicle is fine) and continue if you are able. If you are not able to and you must abandon, to get credit for this partial lap you must be tracking your GPS location on your phone or Garmin (type) unit. You must save this file to Strava and present it to the Event Director when you declare you have abandoned before the official end of your timed event. If you do this then the Event Director will review your Strava ride and credit you with the mileage you rode on the partial lap.

Trains or temporary road closure due to an accident:

If you get stopped by a train or temporary road closure due to an accident: you can turn around and immediately start riding the course in the opposite direction until you feel the road will be cleared when you return, then turn back around and ride back to the same spot. To get credit for any mileage ridden in this scenario - you must be tracking your GPS location on your phone or Garmin (type) unit. When the event is over you must immediately upload the file to Strava and send it to the Event Director and tell them when and where this occurred. Ideally you will hit the  lap timer at the beginning and end of your “detour” so it can be easily seen in Strava analysis..

Event protocol:

All events will start at 7:00am and will ride their respective long loop until there is not enough time to ride another loop - then they will transition to the 6.8 mile loop until their time is finished.

Non-drafting riders let all the Drafting riders go off first.

Non-drafting Rules:

If you are in any non-drafting category, you must honor the “non-drafting zone”. We have adopted the USA Triathlon (USAT) definition of this ‘zone’: as a “rectangular area seven 7 meters long (23 feet) and two 2 meters wide (6.5 feet) surrounding each bicycle”. This will provide a sufficient non-drafting area around each cyclist.

Miscellaneous:

This event is also aligning with the World Record setting standards within World UltraCycling Association (WUCA). This new format also allows all riders to ride until the very end of their timed event. Everyone will be encouraged and allowed to complete the current lap they are on until their time event expires.

** Special Note for Trikes, Handcycles, ElliptiGOs: Due to speed, time, visibility and safety concerns, you will be allowed to ride the 6.8 Mile short-loop for the entire duration of any 6, 12, or 24 hour event if you like. Just tell me you want to do this when you check-in and I’ll assign you a special category number for it in the timing system.

Follow vehicles and crew:

Only riders who choose to ride the historic 50-mile loop (at your own peril) are allowed to have a personal support vehicle somewhere on the course to assist you. These are the rules:

  1. You must provide your contact information and also have the number of the Event Director.
  2. You may not directly follow your rider as that would present a dangerous situation with so many riders on the road. If you are seen doing this during the day, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop.
  3. You may be on the course and stop at a pre-arranged location to hand off food or drink to your rider or offer any other type of assistance they need. It is best to pick one spot and stay there until your rider transitions to the 6.8 mile loop. If possible - riders should plan on  carrying enough food and drink for a 50.5 mile ride.
  4. Your rider may call you if they need mechanical aid and you may drive to, and stop anywhere on the course to offer mechanical aid as long as it is done off the road.
  5. Handoffs from the support vehicle while it is moving are not allowed. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop. 

During the daytime loop, supported riders may have their crew set-up anywhere along the route as long as they are completely off the road and not on private property. They may also set up in the designated area behind Shawnee High School just past the start/finish timing area.

15 & 7-Mile Loop Support rules:

  • Direct follow is not allowed when your rider is on these shorts loop. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop.
  • You may only setup rider pit areas in the High School parking lot
  • Your rider may call you if they need mechanical aid and you may drive to, and stop anywhere on the course to offer mechanical aid as long as it is done off the road.

Where to park your vehicle:

  • There is plenty of space for parking and crew setup behind the School.
  • Preference will be given to self-supported riders to set up as near as possible to the riding path.

Electricity access:

Plan on there being no electrical outlets for you to plug into. I suggest small relatively silent generators or inverters that you can run from your vehicle if you need 110V power.

Unsupported Category:

This means that you are “totally” self-supported. You cannot have anyone help you in any way. If you get in a bad way on the course and need to call for help, you must either abandon and take your mileage at that spot - or change to the Supported Category.

Awards and souvenirs:

Registration fee includes a beautiful forged Calvins medallion especially designed for this event with a 2026 insert. Recognition each event for ALL participants in drafting, non-drafting, supported, unsupported, age-group, gender, and bike categories. There will also be recognition for Overall in all main categories. Awards and recognition ceremonies will be held individually for each event as soon as the results for each event can be tabulated after completion. Award Ceremonies after each event will be held near the start/finish line (or at the Concession Stand Shelter by the football field if raining.)

Accommodations:

  • There are many hotels in and around Springfield where you can stay
  • This is no outdoor camping allowed at the school, but you can park your RV there.

Misc Info:

Both courses used will be surveyed for exact length (to the cm), and all riders will be allowed to ride until their timed event expires, therefore allowing the greatest possible distance for each participant.

WUCA and GWR time and distance records on Surveyed Calvins courses:

Because of alignment with WUCA Record attempt rules, these surveyed courses can also be used to attempt any valid time and distance WUCA record attempt. This attempt cannot however happen simultaneously with the Calvins Challenge event. Contact records@ultracycling.com for more information about a WUCA record attempt. Registration for this must be done at least 21 days prior to your record attempt to allow the pre-attempt documentation to be completed.

Because the courses will be surveyed for exact distance to the cm (also per WUCA Record rules) based on the shortest possible rideable distance, this may vary slightly with what your GPS unit reports. (The surveyed distance is almost always a little shorter) Your final distance will be calculated off of this survey and how many laps you have completed..

Many thanks to the Shawnee School District and especially the principal and athletic director or the High School

Lastly, we are very fortunate in that the Shawnee School District  has graciously allowed us to use their High School for our event again . PLEASE be considerate of the building and the space. Don’t try to gain access to the tracks or the school. Use the time immediately after your event (while you are waiting for the award ceremony) to remove all personal items and all trash from your support area.

Note: Great cleanup job from everyone who attended the 2026 event - You could not even tell we were there - and that is how it should be!

DATE: Saturday May 15-16, 2027

Hosted in the small western town of DeBeque, CO, this is more than just a race—it’s a full-blown Wild West weekend! Cyclists will enjoy a country cookout, campfires, live local music, and free camping within walking distance of the start line. In true western style, it’s a hoedown you don’t want to miss!

The weekend features the Wild Horse Gravel bike races and a 55K and half marathon runs, offering something for every adventurer.

Adding to the exclusivity, The High Lonesome Ranch opens its rugged dirt roads only for this event, giving participants rare access to some of the best-hidden wild-west gravel. Also, the Town of DeBeque offers up free riverside camping for Wild Horse racers, friends and family.

Whether you’re here to crush it on the bike or savor the ride with friends, the focus is on fun. Even the speed demons pause to regroup, soak in the breathtaking views, and enjoy the incredible local treats at our fully stocked feed stations. Choose your weapon, skinny or fat tires. You won't break any records on a mountain bike but it will make for a more enjoyable experience.

Mark your calendar and get ready for an unforgettable weekend of gravel, good times, and western charm! 

 

In addition to a great experience on your bike, each participant will receive:

  • Commemorative t-shirt
  • Refreshments and support throughout the race
  • Pre-ride breakfast & post-ride cookout
  • Bike number with timing chip
  • Opportunity to compete for the podium and purse (prize money is available in the Pro/Open category of the Mustang course only)

In true cycling tradition, the Wild Horse Gravel will take place regardless of weather; therefore refunds will not be provided.

The Farmer's Daughter Gravel Grinder (FDGG) is “the must do spring cycling event in the Northeast.” To celebrate, we've added the Farmer's Granddaughter, a shortened route with no single track/ trail sections! Regardless of which course you ride, you'll be treated to some of the most beautiful scenery in the Northeast, with plenty of climbing, and plenty of fun descents to match. Named after the Chatham Brewery’s Rye IPA born and brewed in Columbia County in beautiful upstate New York, the ride offers a truly grand tour of northern Columbia County and surrounding areas. 

All riders, regardless of route receive  FDGG Swag  and  custom FDGG name plate There will be great food and support along the way, a meal at the finish, and if you're 21 years or older,  you can also reward yourself at the finish with a free pint of Chatham Brewery’s Farmer’s Daughter Rye IPA.

Farmer's Granddaughter Start Time: 9:00 AM

Farmer's Daughter - Course description: The FDGG course is approximately 63 miles long, with about 6,000 feet of climbing - almost entirely on dirt roads with some sections of off-road thrown in. 2 sections will be on single track trails.

A gravel bike or cross bike,  is optimal for the course, and a hard-tail mountain bike would also work well. 

The Farmer's Daughter route has 3 fully supported aid stations, portable toilets, and sweep vehicles. Be sure to carry some food and water as well as spare tubes, tools, and a pump. Be prepared for a challenging, but FUN ride!

Farmer's Daughter Course Map:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/45038404

Farmer's Granddaughter - Course Description   The route is approximately 43 miles in length with 3,700 feet of climbing. Course is the same as FDGG until the single track section at mile 26 (Hand Hollow).  There are NO  SINGLE TRACK TRAILS SECTIONS ON THIS ROUTE!   Riders will pass by 2 of the fully supported aid stations,  including the Bountiful Bread aid station.  Portable toilets and sweep vehicles will be provided. 

A gravel bike or cross bike,  is optimal for the course, and a hard-tail mountain bike would also work well. 

Farmer's Granddaughter Course map: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/45033085

Two  fully supported aid stations, portable toilets, and sweep vehicles will be provided.  Be sure to carry some food and water,  as well as the usual spare tubes, tools, and pump. Be prepared for a challenging, but fun ride!

6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder

Sunday, May 16, 2027 – 10:00 AM Mass Start
Benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation

Join us for the 6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder (REGG)—a scenic day of gravel riding through the beautiful back roads of Geneva, Ohio, all benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.

We’re excited to be back at Red Eagle Distillery for another year of great riding, great company, and great support for a great cause. Riders of all experience levels are welcome, with three route options:

  • 44-mile Classic Gravel Grinder
  • 22.5-mile Sprint Gravel Grinder
  • 12-mile Family Ride

About the Rides

  • Ride hard with friends or enjoy a relaxed cruise—your pace, your adventure.
  • All riders begin together at 10:00 AM in a mass-start, Gran Fondo-style rollout from Red Eagle Distillery.
  • Please note: This is a timed ride with posted results, but it is not a race.
  • New for 2026: Chip timing for all riders, with awards for the top three Female and Male finishers in both the 43-mile and 22.5-mile routes.
  • Expect a mix of gravel, chip seal, dirt, mud, and some pavement (about 55% gravel).
  • Gravel, cyclocross, mountain, single/fixed gear, fat tire, and tandem bikes are welcome. Road bikes are not recommended.
  • E-bikes are permitted but not eligible for awards.
  • All routes will be clearly marked; cue sheets and maps will be available.
  • Official routes will be posted on Ride With GPS:
    • Red Eagle Classic Gravel Grinder – 44 Miles
    • Red Eagle Sprint Gravel Grinder – 22.5 Miles
    • Red Eagle Gravel Family Ride – 12.5 Miles
  • Registered riders will receive Ride With GPS files the week before the event.
  • Roads are open to traffic—please ride safely and obey all traffic laws.
  • Helmets are required; front and rear lights encouraged.
  • Please respect the roads and your fellow riders—no littering.
  • Water & Fuel Stops:
    • 44-mile route: 2 stops
    • 22.5-mile route: 1 stop
  • A SAG vehicle will be on course for rider assistance.

What You Get

  • The pride of riding in one of Northeast Ohio’s premier gravel events—all while supporting AYA (adolescent & young adult) cancer patients through the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.
  • A Red Eagle Gravel beer glass for every registered rider—perfect for your post-ride beverage!
  • Post-ride celebration including:
    • One complimentary drink (yes…beer!)
    • A hot bowl of chili courtesy of Red Eagle Distillery & Black Door Tavern
    • Additional food available for purchase
  • Pre-ordered Red Eagle Gravel Grinder gear will be available for pickup on event day.

No Refund Policy

The Red Eagle Gravel Grinder is a fundraiser for the Steven G. Cancer Foundation and will be held rain or shine. We are unable to offer refunds under any circumstances.

If the event must be canceled, registration fees (minus credit card and BikeReg processing fees) will be refunded. Riders will also have the option to donate their registration to the Foundation. Any cancellation updates will be communicated to participants as promptly as possible.

EventNotes:
The Trans-Sylvania Epic Stage Races offers ala carte style registration, in a series of steps depending on the event and category you enter. Stay where you like, eat what you like, and pay only for what you need. 

 

CHOOSE YOUR RACE CATEGORY Lots of ways to come out and play!

  • Race Solo in the open field, or in your age-group
  • Race Duo with three categories to choose from (female, male or co-ed duo teams)
  • Epic Experience is the cost-effective way to spend time with each other (CLICK HERE for more information.  Shown on our mtb website but is the same information for the gravel.)

Camping:

Arrival: Registration opens at 4:00 p.m. on Thursday

If you are sleeping on the Susquehannock Peninsula camping area you must purchase onsite camping. This includes; sharing a tent with a friend, sleeping on a camp table, sleeping in a roof-top tent, using a hammock, etc.

  • All on-site camping is communal camping, which means you will share a campsite with other campers. Be ready to make some new friends!
  • Campsites are assigned about a week prior to the event. Campsite assignments will be emailed out 2-4 days prior to the start of the event. They will be posted at the entrance gate as well as the registration tent. If you have special requests, please make them heard early!
  • ALL Camping on Susquehannock is primitive camping, there is no electricity, no showers. Lake is a great option though, nearest showers are at 7-Points Beach.
  • Group Camping: You will be assigned a camping spot depending on the size of your group. We cannot guarantee all campers their own group site. Our goals are to have groups seven or larger have their own site, but there are times where we need to combine people and/or groups together. Please make sure your whole group uses the same name so no one gets mixed up or left out of the group. Enter the full group name and not just an acronym under Team/Club/Company on registration. If you do not enter a group name you will be put in individual camping.
  • Individual Camping: If you don't have a group, that's okay! You will share a campsite with other individual campers or be put in with a medium-large sized camp group.
  • There are no specific site reservations at Susquehannock Campground.
  • Once camping sells out, that is it! If someone in your group didn't sign up in time, you can wag your finger at them! Encourage your group to sign up ASAP! On-site camping will sell out.
  • The maximum length for any vehicle parking on-site is 20 feet.  Example; short wheel-base sprinter 144 or pickup truck.

Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century

The event you've always known and loved... just got even better.

Welcome to the next chapter of one of Alabama's favorite gravel traditions. The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is everything you've come to expect—endless quiet dirt roads, Southern hospitality, and an unforgettable day on the bike—but with an exciting new home and an even bigger finish-line celebration.

For 2027, we're moving the start and finish to Historic Downtown Opelika, where race day will kick off with the energy of a community festival. Riders and spectators can enjoy local food trucks, craft beer from Red Clay Brewing Co., handcrafted cocktails from John Emerald Distillery, live music, vendors, and a vibrant downtown atmosphere before and after the ride.

Once you're out on course, it's still the Dirty Deluxe you know and love. We'll feature a 30, 60 and 100-ish mile route that showcases the best red clay roads, rolling countryside, and scenic backroads East Alabama has to offer. Along the way, expect the same welcoming volunteers, well-stocked aid stations, and the laid-back, grassroots feel that's made this event a favorite for over a decade.

We've also added a few fun new awards, expanded post-race festivities, and several surprises we'll be announcing as race weekend approaches.

To preserve the rider experience, registration will once again be limited to 350 participants. When it's full, it's full—so don't wait to claim your spot.

The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is proudly produced by James Bros. Bikes, with proceeds benefiting the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF).

About the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation

The Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF) is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by the owners of James Bros. Bikes after encountering countless abandoned dogs while riding Alabama's backroads.

AARRF exists to support the small, privately operated rescue organizations that work tirelessly to provide sanctuary, medical care, rehabilitation, adoption, and transportation for neglected and abandoned animals throughout Alabama. These rescues fill a critical gap in a state where animal welfare resources are often limited and many county shelter systems remain overwhelmed.

Every dollar generated through the Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century helps AARRF continue its mission of supporting these rescue partners and giving discarded animals a second chance.

When you register, you're not only signing up for an incredible day on some of the best gravel roads in the Southeast—you’re helping change lives, both on two wheels and four paws.

About the MTB 100

For 24 years, the Mohican MTB 100 has attracted riders from all over the world. The race begins in a mass start in downtown Loudonville, Ohio and finishes at Mohican Adventures one mile from downtown. Riders criss-cross three counties along a single loop, climb 10,000 feet, and go pedal-to-pedal with the top pros on this legendary ultra-endurance loop in Northeastern Ohio. The Mohican 100 features both a 100 mile and a 100-kilometer option with six fully stocked aid stations.

2026 Race Recap

More than 500 racers tackled this year's Mohican MTB 100, braving muddy trails and challenging conditions brought on by mid-day storms. Despite the obstacles, participants consistently express their enthusiasm for riding Mohican, where the finish line festivities provide a rewarding conclusion to the adventure. Course Information

Know before you arrive

  • All Race starts, 100 mile, 100k and 50k begin in downtown Loudonville, Ohio beneath a large Mohican MTB 100 Banner and ends at Mohican Adventures (about 1 mile from downtown)
  • 100 mile or 100k loops consists of up to 10,000 feet of climbing along mostly singletrack, double track or dirt roads, spanning three counties through some of the most remote and scenic areas in the rolling hills of Mohican Country.
  • Climbs of nearly a mile, with elevation gains of 300+ feet, rock gardens, streams, and more.
  • The 100-mile course is planned to include five fully stocked and manned aid stations.
  • 100-mile competitors will have the choice of sending drop bags (labeled 1 Gallon Ziplock bag or Hydrapak) to aid stations 2, 3 and 4.  100k can send drop bags to Aid 2 only.
  • Aid stations 1 and 5 are excluded for drop bags.

     

Yield to Horses

Public horse trail

Horses may be traveling along a short section of the Blue Trail from the end of the snowmobile trail, crossing SR97 to CR3234, about five miles past aid station one.

 

Notices have been posted requesting they avoid this section of trail until 1:00 p.m., but this is a public horse trail. If you encounter a horse, YOU MUST stop and walk your bike or pull your bike off the trail to allow them to pass.

 

Horses often view moving bicycles as predators and can panic, causing a danger to the rider. Be sure to talk to the rider as you approach and as they pass since this will help put the horses at ease. If an incident occurs because of your neglect of this rule you may be disqualified.

Aid station information

5 aid stations

There will be 5 aid stations for the Mohican 100. 100-mile racers are permitted drops at your choice of aid stations 2, 3, 4. 100k racers can drop at 2.

Aid station items

Water, Coca Cola, PB&J's, fruit, (typically cut Banana's, oranges, watermelon), cookies, trail mix, and chips. Hammer Nutrition Products: Hammer Heed Electrolyte drink, Racer's should bring their own Hammer Gel’s, however; there will some hammer gels available at the aid stations.

Drop bags

100-mile racers are permitted drops at your choice of aid stations 2, 3, 4. 100k racers can drop at 2. If you require special foods, it is recommended that you include them in your drop bags. Drop bags are located in your race packet and can be placed in the bins located at packet pickup on Friday AND Saturday morning. All drops will head to aid stations at 7am.

  • Finish Line cut off for all racers: 9:30pm

Level playing field

Racers are not allowed to accept parts, including wheel sets and spare bikes, or any supplies not available to ALL racers from support crews and/or spectators at ANY time. This includes aid stations that allow crew access. Only parts and/or supplies included in drop bags will be allowed or cables, tubes, tires, etc. offered by aid station volunteers to ALL racers. RACERS RECEIVING SPARE PARTS, BIKES, WHEEL SETS, ETC. FROM SUPPORT CREWS MAY BE DISQUALIFIED.

Direction to aid stations

Aid Station 3, Brinkhaven Bridge of Dreams, is off limits to family and crews. Directions and parking for all other stations can be found here.

Since its inception in 2006, the National Ultra Endurance Race Series (NUE) has elevated the sport of ultra-endurance Mountain Biking to the national stage. It is dedicated to providing a level playing field for ALL riders, professionals and amateurs alike! No USAC or any other license is required. To become eligible for National Series rankings and rewards, racers need only complete THREE events to receive a national ranking and qualify for series awards. The Mohican MTB 100 has been a NUE series race from day one of NUE.

Welcome to the FINGER LAKES FRESHET! 

freshet /freSHet/ noun - the springtime rush of fresh water from melting snow.

 

BIG NEWS:  New DATE for 2027- Grand Depart is May 29, 2027!

Also, in 2027, all routes will be in the reverse direction from previous years!

This is a casual, unofficial, unsanctioned, and unsupported gravel bikepacking group or solo ride starting and ending in Stewart Park, Ithaca, NY, homeland of the Gayogohó:no people.  We have four routes available from 40ish miles up to 500ish miles!  The pace you set is your own, so take your time or ride fast, it's your call.  The terrain between lakes and around the southern tier of the Finger Lakes tends to be very hilly, so expect plenty of climbing, sometimes on the order of about 100' per mile, or 1,000' per 10 miles in the more rugged sections.  This is especially the case as we have sought out quieter gravel roads through state forest lands, as well as single track sections to spice things up.  The routes are certainly challenging, and less than half the riders completed it in our first two years ('25 and '26 results are below). Sometimes that is due to weather adding extra challenge (year one), and other times, it is mechanicals or what have you, but do not fear, many friends are near to provide moral support.  We avoid traffic as much as possible in our routing, but that means you can also expect some rough gravel, some singletrack, and some steep snowmobile trails.  We have eliminated most of the hike-a-bike spots in favor of rideable sections, but we've kept in some tough sections as they connect areas nicely.  On most routes there will be a little bit of walking.  We'd rather hike-a-bike than share the road with cars, to be honest.  A burly gravel bike or a svelte mountain bike would be ideal.  We'd recommend knobby 38-60 mm tires.  

This ride follows the self-supported ethics of other bikepacking events like The Adirondack Trail Ride, Vermont Super 8, Catskill Bikepacking Route, or the Tour Divide – meaning it's an unmarked route, with no sag wagon, no planned feed stations, etc, but you can utilize any publicly available services. And there probably won't be anyone at the finish line other than your friends and family.  If you wish to be “compete” for a fast time, the rules of self-supported races apply, where you can't receive aid from friends or family, but may utilize food, lodging, repair stations, as long as they are publicly available resources.  Otherwise, if you're touring it at your own slow pace, “cheat” as much as you like to ease the time.  

You can certainly ride fast – but we also encourage riders to go slow and ride together in groups. To this end, we will identify a group campsite or two, the previous two years, groups of riders stayed at event director Paul's place, and we'll probably do that again, but the routes will all be in the REVERSE direction this year.  Route maps will be updated around Dec ‘26 - Jan ’27 to reflect the new directions, and some minor route tweaks to optimize the experience will be added, as usual. And regardless of which route you sign up for, you can switch routes if you're feeling more or less ambitious on the day of the ride.

Riders who wish to push themselves physically and mentally may choose to do so, but will need to agree to be safe about it and be respectful of everyone they encounter en route – especially on rail trails where cyclists need to yield to all other users. If you want friends and family to be able to follow your progress in real-time, we'll have the routes on Trackleaders and facilitate SPOT rental (about $85) or the PING phone app (about $15). But riders aren't required to do this unless you want your official time posted or you hope to set an official FKT (Fastest Known Time) for a route. It's the only feasible way for us to fairly and accurately record times. As a bonus, the Trackleaders webpage holds an archived event replay for all tracked events, where you can follow along with the race and ride flow!  What a fun record!  

In our first two years, the event was held the first weekend in May, but for a few reasons we are shifting the date in 2027 for a grand depart on Memorial Day weekend, Saturday, May 29, 2027.   More details on routes, parking, camping, GPS tracking, and other logistics will be sent to registered riders as the Freshet approaches. Also, all registered riders who sign-in will receive a Freshet 2027 handmade print in the mail.

Photos, including Rigs of the Freshet portraits, can be found on our Instagram page: https://www.instagram.com/fingerlakesfreshet/

Past results:

In 2026, out of 75 registered riders, we had 31 intrepid finishers (listed below). Full replays can be found at https://trackleaders.com/freshet26. These were the courses in 2026:

In 2025, out of 52 registered riders, only 17 courageous riders finished (listed below). Much fun was had, despite the rain and tough conditions, and it was a beautiful green spring ride, abounding with water, camaraderie, wildflowers, plenty of mud, some sublime moments, and some challenge. Kudos to TJ, who rode from his house for a total of 190 miles! Full replay here:  https://trackleaders.com/freshet25. IMPORTANT EVENT DAY INFORMATION

There are many important details to ensure the safety of our riders and volunteers. Please read everything in it's entirety.

Post-Ride Ammentity: Living Water Showers will be set up and offering FREE showers to riders post event. The showers are first come first serve. KNOW BEFORE YOU GO!!

Please note: No biking shoes will be allowed inside of the fire hall on ride day. Please plan accordingly with a change of shoes.

 

Parking & Traffic Flow – Please be sure to carefully follow the traffic patterns as they may have changed from previous years. There is plenty of free additional parking in the grass once the asphalt lot fills up. Please be aware of your surroundings when entering and leaving the fire hall to make sure there are no cyclists around you.

 

COURSE NOTES:

 

The Century route will be marked with WHITE arrows, the Metric Century with GREEN arrows, the Club Ride with ORANGE, and the Family Ride with PINK arrows.

Please take a cue sheet with you before you leave. These will also be available at the Fire Hall.

 

Ride with GPS: You can create a free Ride with GPS account by visiting https://ridewithgps.com/. All routes are uploaded and viewable/downloadable on the app. 

 

WHAT TO BRING:

  •  Please bring an ID (required for alcoholic beverages) and money for additional drink tickets, merch, etc. (please avoid using cash)

  • Lawn chairs and/or a blanket to use while enjoying the finish line party.
  • A change of clothes. We will have Living Water Showers set up at the Finish Line Party and you are welcome to use their shower stalls to rinse off post- ride. All towels and toiletries included!! 
  • A water bottle. All rest stops will have 5 gallon jugs to refill with water and/or Gatorade. 
  • Your phone (fully charged is helpful!)
  • Your helmet. Helmets MUST be worn at all times. 
  • Repair kit that includes an extra tube that fits your bike.

RIDING SAFELY:

 

1) Please be sure your bike is in good, working order before you arrive. If in doubt, take your bike to a shop to get a tune-up. We recommend The Bike Doctor, The Bicycle Escape, or Blue Ridge Bicycles. Their mechanics will be available on Saturday at the event for last minute checks such as pumping up tires, patching holes, etc and they will be stationed at some of the rest stops. 

 

2) You MUST wear a helmet. Riders without helmets will NOT be allowed to ride or will be removed from the course if seen riding without a helmet.

 

3) Do not ride more than two abreast. Many of these roads are narrow country roads. Please do not take up a whole lane of traffic by riding more than two abreast. SAG vehicles have been told to break this up if they see it on course. When riding through Gettysburg National Military Park on the Century route please ride SINGLE FILE. 

 

4) Obey ALL traffic laws. If you see a red light or STOP sign...you must stop! The roads are not closed, and you will be riding with vehicles on the road. Riders seen breaking traffic laws will be removed from the course.

 

REST STOPS:

 

There will be a total of 6 rest stops on the course. Century riders will pass all 6, the Metric will pass 4, and the Club Ride will pass 2. When you are entering or leaving a rest stop, make sure you know your surroundings and signal or tell people what you are doing to avoid an accident. Make sure to thank our great rest stop sponsors/volunteers who are out there to support you!

 

Water, PowderVitamin, peanut butter & jelly sandwiches, granola bars, and bananas will be at every stop and each stop will have their own special treats for riders. Rest stop times will also be printed on the cue sheets.  

 

There is a small “rest stop” along the 10 mile family route in Heritage Farm Park. There will be some snacks and sodas for the participants.

EventName: The CCAP's Breakaway Benefit Cycling Festival
EventNotes:
Welcome to the 2027 Breakaway Benefit Cycling Festival, hosted at Norbrook Farm Brewery.      
The cornerstone fundraising event for the CT Cycling Advancement Program

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

**Exiting Highlights for 2027**

A NEW road ride option

A premium gravel ride with 5 timed segments

Mountain biking at CT's best privately owned trail system

Check out this year's routes HERE

AWESOME Fundraising Awards…like our 2026 ICE CREAM JERSEY

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •


The Breakaway Benefit Cycling Festival is the cornerstone fundraiser for the Connecticut Cycling Advancement Program (CCAP) and directly helps us provide hundreds of kids with access to cycling and cycling teams all across the state. The CCAP started in 2013 and has grown to be a national leader in the development of youth cycling programs with teams in schools and regions across the state. In the last twelve years, we've served thousands of kids and orchestrated hundreds of events in over 50 towns. Annually, over 350 youth riders participate across 40 programs in mountain biking, road cycling, and cyclocross. Additionally, the CCAP hosts over 25 youth race events and skills clinics annually. With your support, you're helping create more school and municipality-based youth cycling programs and helping the CCAP get thousands more kids on bikes, so please join us on this fun-filled day, pedaling bikes and enjoying time with family!

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

Fundraising Awards

All Breakaway Benefit attendees are eligible for AMAZING fundraising awards, which are compounding, meaning the more you raise, the more you get! Our top prize is oh-so-worth it and people will be jealous of your incredible style for years to come.  To be clear, this is not a fundraising minimum. 

Take a look at last year's Fundraising Tips Packet (2027 coming soon) to see all of the sweet CCAP prizes you can earn by going that extra mile in fundraising for Connecticut's youth cycling. Hint: it's all in our famous limited-edition ice cream design.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

This is the Breakaway Benefit:

  • Gravel and Mountain Bike Rides for ALL: Enjoy Connecticut's most beautiful and scenic roads during fully supported rides of different lengths. Our Gravel Sampler is perfect for a beginner to novice rider and is fully marked, so there is no need for a navigation device if you don't have one. The Big Scoop offers fun for riders of all abilities but is a bit longer - ride at your own pace or have fun cruising around with friends - just remember, roads are open to traffic.  Mountain bikers, will be riding the beautiful trails at Norbrook Farm Brewery with ride lengths of multiple distances; expect routes as short as 5 miles and as long as 12. We will have two coach-led routes so need to memorize the trails.
  • A Theme to Remember: Check out this last year's famed and unique Breakaway Benefit Ice Cream Kit, which will serve as inspiration for all of our other swag items available at different levels (more info below in the fundraising packet)
  • Festival: This isn't just a ride! We'll have a team tent zone, kids' games, product vendors, and more bike-focused fun to keep you entertained throughout the day. CCAP staff, along with a DJ/live music, will be on hand to lead the fun!
  • Delicious Food and Drink: Riders are welcome to enjoy a light, pre-ride arrangement of pastries and coffee, then we will kick off the ride with a quick ceremony of Fundraising Awards (including top fundraiser and top junior fundraiser)! Enjoy the ride and then join us for lunch, a live DJ, and games to celebrate their riding, fundraising, and accomplishments.
  • Want to volunteer? Please visit our Volunteer Page to sign up! All volunteers will receive complimentary breakfast, and lunch after the ride! No fundraising is required for volunteers, however, it is encouraged. For volunteer questions, please reach out to volunteer@ctcyclingadvancement.com.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

The Breakaway Benefit Ride is dedicated to the memory of David Hoyle; and honors him with our ever-changing ice cream design. As the Executive Director of CCAP, Dave was tirelessly working to provide kids and their families with the opportunity to ride bikes. He was an advocate for the sport, a healthy lifestyle, and embodied the highest level of humility and kindness to all whom he came across. He will forever be in our hearts.

Please join us in celebrating Dave and the wonderful impact he had on the Connecticut cycling community with a fun, family-filled day on bikes!

Those who want to fundraise in memory of Dave and ride are encouraged to do so by signing up for any ride distance and rising above and beyond the fundraising requirement! Those who DO NOT wish to ride but want to attend are encouraged to volunteer or sign up for the non-cyclist fundraising category.

#ridelikedave

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • •

Timed Segment Details

Individual Timing Details: The Breakaway Benefit Gravel rides are as competitive as you want them to be, rip it, ride it, or just have fun. Participation is not required to ride. Keep in mind, this is not a race; it's a fundraising ride. Roads, while lightly trafficked, are open to traffic, so riders MUST abide by all local traffic laws (don't run stop signs, cross the center-line of the road, etc). Details for fondo style timed segments:

  • 5 Timed Segments (1-2 Miles in length)
  • Results are the lowest cumulative time through all segments - riders must complete all 5 segments to be eligible for awards
  • Segment Start/Finish will be marked with signage
  • Top 3 Men / Women awards for Big Scoop Gravel
  • Winner recognition for Individual Junior Boys/Girls (U19); 45+ Men/Women; 55+ Men/Women for Big Scoop Gravel
  • Breakaway Gravel Sampler segment results are for fun
  • Preview timed segments here
  • Team Competition - Bring your Teammates (more details below)!


Team Competition Details: There will be a team competition. To be eligible, each member must register with their team affiliation. Team membership will be determined based on the ‘Team/Club/Company’ field during BikeReg checkout. Please ensure all team members use the same name for your team.

Rules are as follows: 
  • Men and Women categories.
  • Men must have a minimum of four riders; women must have a minimum of three riders.
  • There is no maximum number of riders one team can have. Bring everyone.
  • Only riders who enter and complete the Big Scoop course and all five timed segments by 2 p.m. will be scored
  • The time of the fourth fastest rider of each men’s team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team’s result.
  • Only the time of the third fastest rider of each women’s team in each segment will be used for scoring. The aggregate of those scores will be tabulated for the team’s result.
  • Any combination of riders on a team can be scored. For example, a team may have different riders scoring in each segment.
  • The overall individual results have no bearing on the team competition.
  • Only one men’s and one women’s team will be awarded the team competition.

About This Event
The Rotary Club of Grass Valley and Bright Futures for Youth of Nevada County invite you to participate in our Twelfth  Annual Gold Country Challenge. The event includes a half metric, 55 and 75 mile ride, and a 100 mile Century tour of the beautiful Gold country region of Northern California.    And now we have the  17 mile Wolf Creek Challenge for new riders.  The rides are fully supported by friendly volunteers, fantastic rest stops, support vehicles, and well-marked routes.

After your ride, included with your registration, you can relax, visit with other riders, and enjoy a hearty dinner and entertainment at the Fairgrounds in Grass Valley. Invite your family to the BBQ.  Beer is on us.

Donations: The ride benefits the youth programs supported by Rotary - scholarships, youth leadership experiences, student exchange programs, support of Lyman Gilmore, Union Hill Middle School, and Chicago Park School and other programs.  

            This year you can ride free.  By going to Pledge Reg your donations will benefit Bright Futures for Youth and their youth support programs.  By raising $300 from friends we will refund your registration fee.

Thank you 
The Rotary Club of Grass Valley and Bright Futures for Youth thank you for helping to support our projects focused on the youth of our community.  Again Thanks James and Cheryl

We have a strict no refunds policy.  If you are a no show, take comfort in knowing that your fee is a donation and is going to help fund local youth programs.

EventName: 3 Feet Cycling Unbound Gravel SAG Support for Hire 2027 - Emporia, KS
EventNotes:
3 Feet Cycling will once again be offering SAG Support services in Emporia, KS June 6, 2027 supporting the 200-mile and 100-mile events. Our services include local knowledge of the course prior to race day, answering any questions you may have, drop bag services, minor mechanical services, power washer, water, soft drinks, nutrition, cooling towels and encouragement to get you to the finish line.  All you need to focus on is riding your bike to the finish line and 3 Feet Cycling will take care your race day needs.  

If your day doesn’t go as planned, it’s ok! One of the many 3 Feet Cycling team members will pick you up and drive you to the finish line in Emporia. Plan on bringing your phone with you and the 3 Feet Cycling SAG number will be provided during bag drop. If you have someone local that is waiting for you, we encourage you to always share your location on your phone or when the phone signal is available. 

Our team members have been providing support for riders since 2016 in the Flint Hills and many have completed the 100-mile and 200-mile events along with other gravel endurance races. Our services speak for itself, and we’ve been fortunate enough to support many podium finishers in several age groups and overall winners. We continue to refine and improve our process of what we offer, and we love to support all our riders and listening to their race day stories. 

**there are no refunds of fees if you choose to defer or not participate. We do offer to defer your support to the following year if you would like. You need to email us by May 29th, 2026 to be issued a credit for the following years support. 

Watch our team in action at Checkpoint 1 in Eureka, KS in 2022. https://youtu.be/BMMbN485tzs

 

Rules require you to have someone available to pick you up if you abandon. Event organizers will NOT come pick you up. 3 Feet Cycling is not an official partner of Lifetime or Unbound Gravel.

The Great Descent Presented By L.A. Tourist

NOT FOR BEGINNERS

WARNING: This event is not for everyone, the route covers tight single track, steep, exposure and technical sections.

The Great Descent is the mountain bike race LA needed. A true mountain adventure For all the mountain bike junkies, are you down to descend 10,000ft of elevation while finding your way along jagged cliffs , thru creeks and along jungle brush.

This route will cover some of our epic mountain bike routes running 50 miles with 10,000ft of descending and 5,000ft of climbing. 

This is a point to point route that starts out at the highest peak we could find that still has great single track and ends all the way back at Let's Ride Cyclery.

finish address is 1819 W Burbank Blvd, Burbank, CA, 91506
 

We have routed an epic one way route that is 90% dirt and only 10% paved.

 Start location is 34.34363° N, 117.98321° W, Race starts at 8am, check in will start at 7am

It is on you to get to the starting line, we do not have a shuttle van yet. Make plans to be dropped off or to have a ride to pick up your car from the start.

The Rules

 

  • This is a set route you will need to follow and there will be a time cutoff, we cant wait forever for you to finish.

  • You must ride the full route exactly, and under your own power,  no catching a ride.  At the finish we will be checking all finishers gps info to verify completion of the route.

  • There is no parking at Let's Ride Cyclery, please use the side streets behind the shop or make plans to be dropped off and picked up.  

  • The bike you start off on is the bike you finish on, no changing bikes allowed.

  • There is no sag vehicle to pick you up and take you home.   Have a plan and tell someone. 

  •  NO E-Bikes

  •  All registrations are FINAL, No Refunds.

  • You can transfer to another rider during the transfer window only, this Must be done before event date, Thank you for your understanding.
